contracts.title: 1.13 · A start that fails ends the app instead of lingering half-started
contracts.description: A failure after Electron is ready, before the app has registered its handlers or started its updater, is logged and ends the app with exit code 1, so it never holds the single-instance lock with a window that can read nothing (sighting 2026-10-03: 13 hours of "No handler registered").

contracts.title: 1.14 · The window keeps drawing through the machine's GPU resets: repeated GPU process crashes never block the app from WebGL, so a lost globe is restored instead of staying white until a restart
contracts.description: The owner's laptop (Adreno X1-85) has Windows reset its GPU about ten times a day (LiveKernelEvent 141). Chromium, by default, blocks a page from 3D APIs after a GPU crash it blames on the page, and disables WebGL after three GPU process crashes; either leaves the globe white with its nameplates until the app restarts. The app starts with both blocks off.

contracts.title: 1.15 · Started with --callback-check, the app reports each sign-in callback a later start hands it, and whether it reached the sign-in session, without opening a window or its library
contracts.description: CI's proof that a storytree-auth callback deep link reaches the running instance (second-instance delivery on Windows and Linux, open-url on macOS) without a live WorkOS sign-in. The first instance holds the single-instance lock and prints one line per callback; a build with no sign-in says the callback arrived but no session takes it. The token exchange is not part of the promise.

contracts.title: 1.16 · A page operation a story declares reaches that story's answer in the main process, with the page's arguments
contracts.description: Each story declares its page operations once (the bridge method and the channel it travels on); the frame builds the page's bridge methods and the main process's handlers from that one declaration, so a call from the page arrives at the story's answer with its arguments and returns its result (ADR-0649 thin frame).

contracts.title: 1.17 · The tray, the window and the packaged app wear the mark: the tray and window in the night colourway on a dark taskbar and the day colourway otherwise, following a change while running; the installer and app bundle in the day colourway
contracts.description: Arc arc_c436976edbfa, increment_7d2ab0a11543. The icons are the mark's package's own rendering (@storytree/mark), never a picture held by the app. The tray reads the operating system's taskbar setting (Electron's shouldUseDarkColorsForSystemIntegratedUI, else shouldUseDarkColors). Fixed-colour files (.ico for Windows and the NSIS installer, .icns for macOS) use the day colourway. The tray's tooltip still names the build.

capabilities.title: 2 · Storytree projects
capabilities.description: The app lists the storytree projects in its database and shows one at a time. Its always-visible, full-width top app bar holds only a gear at the right. The gear opens a large centred overlay with Projects, Settings, Updates and Help sections. Projects moves the whole app to another project in place; Settings mounts the agent link's per-user panel, Updates mounts the app's existing update status, and Help mounts app-setup's existing help surface. The separate arcs-only bar sits below the app bar and the forest starts below both. This capability also decides which project is on show when the app opens.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Projects in the gear overlay lists every project, with the one on show selected. Choosing another project switches the forest and closes the overlay; a failed choice shows its reason inside Projects and leaves the list available for retry.
contracts.description: Mounted evidence: packages/app/evidence/mounted-allocation/prove.mjs runs the actual Desktop renderer through the shared capture kit. It checks listed/selected projects, a refused choice with retry still available, successful replacement and menu closure. The database bridge is a stand-in; project choice uses the real App action in a throwaway home. Node/browser functions are measured separately through matching source maps under ADR-0838; this is not native Electron or live database acceptance.

contracts.title: 2.2 · The list is read again every three seconds, including while empty; a first project appears without restarting, unchanged reads leave the surface alone, and closing the page stops polling.

2.3 · Reopening follows the latest successful explicit project choice, whether made in the picker or by saying yes to setup. A newer picker choice supersedes an older setup choice, and a newer setup choice supersedes an older picker choice. `--project` wins on launch and becomes the remembered choice when that project exists. A remembered project that has gone falls back to the first; an unknown explicit project is named as missing.

2.4 · After a successful setup yes, the chosen project is durably recorded and becomes the project on show on the next refresh, or on reopening. The last successfully recorded yes wins even when several setups complete between reads or while the window is closed. A project-list read never overwrites an explicit choice, including one recorded while that read is in flight; discovering a name alone does not count as choosing it (ADR-0657 D3).
2.5 · With no projects, the app tells the user to add a folder as a project from the gear menu (Projects → Add project…), or run `storytree doctor --set-up <name>` in the folder.

2.6 · The gear opens a full-size centred overlay below the always-visible app bar, with space around it at wide and narrow window sizes. Clicking the gear again, pressing Escape, the Close button or clicking the backdrop closes it and returns keyboard focus to the gear. While open, keyboard focus stays within the overlay and its reachable gear, and the app behind it is inert; dismissal does not also activate the forest or close the arc drawer.

2.7 · The gear overlay has Projects, Settings, Updates and Help sections. The app owns the overlay frame, project switcher and existing Check for updates surface; the agent link mounts its existing per-user Settings panel; app-setup mounts its existing Help surface, including its first-run offer. Settings and updates retain their existing reader, writer and action behaviour. The section navigation has room to grow as settings are added.

2.8 · An always-visible full-width 48 px app bar holds only a 36 px gear at the right. A separate full-width 48 px arcs-only bar sits directly below it, with no project name. The forest and its controls start below both bars at 96 px, and the arc drawer opens below them. With the overlay closed, the forest receives pointer input below the bars or open drawer. The backdrop click that closes the overlay is consumed; subsequent forest input works. The existing data-state and data-drew smoke readings remain valid.
2.9 · A capture settles each requested animation frame before measuring or taking a picture
contracts.description: The shared capture settle helper requests a globe redraw, when the observation hook is present, then awaits that animation frame before requesting the next. It awaits 12 frames by default, accepts an explicit count including zero, and works on pages without a globe hook.

reported.note: The real Chrome regression and existing runner lifecycle test both pass after invoking the serialized frame loop; verified explicit 3, default 12, zero, and no-hook 2 completed animation frames.

contracts.title: 2.10 · A capture names a seed story's file by the package the seed's own story title gives, from a shared seed, so a later rename of the live package cannot desync it
contracts.description: The capture kit's captureSeed gives a fresh copy of a shared, refreshable library snapshot; seedFile names a story's file as packages/<packageOf(the seed's title)>/<path>, the key the globe draws it under, and fails naming the seed's stories when the story is absent (increment_4ed3852f2216, friction_b97f2a2712fc).

contracts.title: 2.11 · The empty page shows storytree's mark drawn in the page theme's own colours, light or dark, from no file
contracts.description: Arc arc_c436976edbfa, increment_7d2ab0a11543. The mark is @storytree/mark's master drawing with its four roles set to the page's CSS variables (--mark-ocean, --mark-land, --mark-tree, --mark-leaf), which the desktop page's stylesheet sets from its own light and dark colours; no tile is drawn, the page is the canvas.

contracts.title: 2.12 · A capture's stand-in bridge opens the page with the first-run guide already seen, so it pictures the globe; a capture of the guide itself opts back in to a first launch
contracts.description: Inputs: a capture installing the shared fake bridge (directly or through runCapture), optionally with guide: "unseen". Outputs: before the page's scripts run, storytree:setup:guide-seen:v1 reads exactly "yes" (as app-setup's guideOffered requires), or is left unset when the capture asks for the guide. Remedies friction_60eb9cc7a640.

capabilities.title: 3 · Surfaces
capabilities.description: The app's window hosts the surfaces for the project on show: the forest, which the app opens on (until it lands, today's plain list), with the arc surface as an overlay that the forest hosts. The page cannot reach the database, so the app carries everything a surface reads to it, and tells the surfaces when the project changes.

contracts.title: 3.1 · The page can ask the app for the library's changes and the agent log's new lines since a point, for the project on show, and only newer ones come back.
3.2 · A name that is not a project is refused, and never created.
3.3 · The smoke check, pointed at the surface on show, passes only if that surface says it drew every story and capability of the project.
3.4 · The page can ask the app for a story's or capability's shelf of front covers, and for the artifacts that link to an artifact, for the project on show.

3.5 · The page can ask the app for the context readings of named sessions in the project on show (agent link 9.5, 9.8), each parsed from the transcript records in the shared log, with no access to the machine the session ran on (ADR-0749 D3); a session with none named reads as an absence, and a name that is not a project is refused.

3.6 · The page can ask the app for a session's window in the project on show (agent link 9.10), or several sessions' in one ask that reads the log once, parsed from the transcript records in the shared log, with no access to the machine the session ran on (ADR-0749 D3); a session with none named reads as an absence.

3.7 · The Surfaces menu lists every surface with its switch and its settings; a surface switched off is saved to the settings file and reads back off, and one that follows it goes off with it; switching an always-on or unknown surface, or to an unknown choice, is refused with its reason and the file is untouched.
contracts.description: ADR-0750's Surfaces menu: what the menu shows and how a switch persists. ADR-0838 D4: its view and switches gain a contract their existing tests carry. Mounted evidence packages/app/evidence/mounted-allocation/prove.mjs checks real Desktop renderer Arcs/Library unmounting after saved switches, reload persistence, Arcs remounting and the App 3.3 census, using real settings actions in a throwaway home and a stand-in database bridge. Suppressing the frame redraw callback fails the mounted assertion. Node/browser execution is measured separately with matching source maps; it allocates App/frame code only.

reported.note: Restored source and cleanup at d8bdc26d: real shared Desktop renderer capture passes persisted Arcs/Library off, reload, Arcs remount and complete project census. Node harness and browser renderer functions measured separately by source maps. Evidence packages/app/evidence/mounted-allocation; fake database bridge and throwaway settings home; not native Electron acceptance.

contracts.title: 3.8 · The page can ask the app for the project's standing delegations
contracts.description: For the project on show, the page can ask for the register its library keeps as the definition "Standing delegation"; a project without one answers with none (agent link 7.6).

contracts.title: 3.9 · After an app start, context readings and single or batched session windows take only the requested sessions’ latest transcript references from the activity log; the bytes read do not grow with the project’s activity history.

reported.note: Final full pnpm gate passed. Typecheck, all 21 test units, and plan edges passed; guidance not run because no roles or guidance notes changed. Startup egress context/windows/window: short 5354/3396/2754 bytes; long 5416/3458/2816, a 62-byte increase despite 20,413,139 bytes of old activity and fat old/latest reference lines.

contracts.title: 3.10 · After a restart the app reuses stored transcript records and fetches only appended records, preserving token counts, composition, historical openings, compactions and kept segments; retention keeps the final readings before raw records expire.
3.11 · The app reads the folders this machine imports for the project on show, so its survey draws the project's mapped stories; a name that is not a project is refused
contracts.description: ADR-0993 D2: the survey reads a mapped story only from a folder this machine imports. The app passes them to the forest's code survey.

capabilities.title: 4 · Updates
capabilities.description:
The app keeps itself up to date by itself: on the owner's machine it runs from its own copy of merged main, notices new merges within a few minutes, and rebuilds and restarts itself in the background, so it never runs unmerged work and nobody rebuilds it by hand. Check for updates in the top-right gear asks that same merged-main updater to check now and shows the running build and its progress or failure. A ready build waits with the window open until no seed or start-up or daily snapshot is being written. A checkout explains that it does not update itself. Installed apps select releases from their own channel: development follows each merged release; stable follows only the owner-pinned existing build (ADR-0871). As built (increment_aca4e6853237): an installed app's downloaded release waits for a quiet moment (packages/app whenToInstall: ten minutes after launch, ten minutes without window input or agent activity from a session that has not ended), because a first install was replaced 17 seconds after setup said the app was open (packages/app-setup/evidence/acceptance, F1). The gear answers from the release updater in an installed app, marks itself with a dot while an update is pending, and its Restart to update installs at once. A seed or snapshot still holds any restart, including one requested from the gear. The owner accepted contracts 4.4 and 4.7's wording for this on 2026-09-29 (a question).

As built (increment_c3e1441890f9, contract 4.12): installed release updates read named, independent run holds under the app home/update-holds before each automatic installation. packages/app/src/updates/hold-run.mjs wraps a foreground command, publishes its hold before launch, removes it on return and preserves its exit code. Holds expire after the requested positive duration, at most six hours; overlapping runs do not release one another. Downloads continue, the pending status names the run, and the user's Restart to update still overrides holds while respecting seed writes and snapshots. The standalone wrapper and usage/proof are in packages/app/evidence/update-hold. No laptop acceptance run is part of this implementation.


As built (increment_402e76453e34, contract 4.17): the follow-main updater start-checks each new build before it may restart into it (apps/desktop/src/main/start-check.ts, wrapping follow-main's build through mainUpdates' update option). The build is started with --start-check, which goes only as far as registering the main process's handlers and exits 0: no library, no network, so a library on Cloud SQL or a local Postgres the running app holds never holds back a good build. A check that does not exit 0 within 60 s fails the build as 4.2 does, and that commit is remembered and not rebuilt. Lifecycle 1.13: run()'s rejection now ends the app (exit 1) instead of leaving it half-started holding the single-instance lock.

contracts.title: 4.1 · When merged main moves, the app is built at main's new commit beside the one running, and work not merged to main is never run.
4.2 · A build that fails leaves the running app as it is.

4.4 · An installed Windows app checks for a newer published release offered by its own release channel, downloads and verifies it, and installs it only at a quiet moment: not in the first ten minutes after a launch, not while the window has been used or an agent session has worked in the last ten minutes, and never while a library seed or project snapshot is being written. The user can install it from the gear without waiting for a quiet moment, but seeds and snapshots still hold the restart with the window open and the update pending. Installing stops its database and restarts through the installer into the new app using the same lifecycle handoff as the development updater.

reported.note: Final pnpm gate passes: installed menu and automatic updates stay pending while snapshots run, including snapshots beginning during the quiet read; retry uses the existing download and restarts once.

contracts.title: 4.5 · A failed release check or download leaves the app running and can be retried; equal and older releases never replace it, concurrent checks share one download, and quitting stops updates.
4.6 · Releases contain only work merged to main and verified on all three systems; every later main build has a higher version, and a rerun cannot replace a newer published release.
4.3 · After each update, the app that follows merged main checks its own verified health
contracts.description: After restarting into a new merged-main build, the app runs `pnpm check:own-health` from that running slot in the background, against its own library. Its window and database remain available. The check joins the running app's database through `appLibraryServer` with `writes: true`, holding the writing lock so an update cannot restart the app while the check runs. The check's output and failures go to `[home] (or the same file under `STORYTREE_HOME`). A failed check never stops the app and is tried again at the next update. Reopening the same build does not repeat the attempt. When the `library` setting names a Cloud SQL instance, the app runs no check and records nothing: CI's run on main is the one writer of the shared library's verified health (ADR-0744 D3), and the app's log says so in one line. This contract applies to the app that follows merged main; installed releases do not run checkout scripts.

contracts.title: 4.7 · Check for updates in the gear checks now, using the same updater as the automatic check: merged main where the app follows main, published releases where it is installed. Concurrent requests share the work. If no newer build is needed, the menu says the app is up to date and identifies the running build.

4.8 · The menu shows when a new build is building, ready or restarting. A ready build updates and restarts the app through the existing lifecycle, waiting with the window open while a seed writes the library or a start-up or daily project snapshot is being written, including when the user asks from the menu; waiting neither rebuilds the ready commit nor starts a second restart.

reported.note: Final pnpm gate passes: startup and daily snapshots hold automatic and menu main updates with the old window open, then reuse the ready build for one restart.

contracts.title: 4.9 · A failed manual update check or build shows its reason, leaves the running app alone, and can be retried from the gear.
4.10 · When the app was started from a checkout rather than a runtime slot, Check for updates explains that it does not update itself; the request neither fetches a build nor restarts the app.

4.11 · Setting up the app that follows main refuses while the app is running, naming its process; otherwise it builds merged main in the runtime folder and starts the app from that build, in the background unless asked to show its window
contracts.description: `pnpm app:follow-main` (ADR-0637 D2): the one-off setup of the app that follows merged main never replaces a build a running app may be using; "running" is the app's database owner process being alive.

contracts.title: 4.12 · A named acceptance run can hold automatic release installation until it releases its hold or a finite ceiling expires; overlapping runs keep independent holds. Downloads continue, and an explicit Restart to update still installs once no seed or project snapshot is being written.

4.13 · The user chooses when a downloaded release may install itself: whenever quiet (the default), only inside their daily quiet hours, or never on its own (manual only); the quiet-moment rule still applies inside the hours, and their own Restart to update installs in every mode once no seed or project snapshot is being written.
contracts.description: ADR-0871 D2. The choice is kept in the app's home and survives a restart; a quiet-hours window may cross midnight; an unreadable or missing choice reads as the default.

contracts.title: 4.14 · The gear's Updates section shows which install choice is on and, for quiet hours, when the next automatic install may happen; changing it there saves it, and a refused change shows its reason and keeps the old choice
contracts.description: ADR-0871 D2: the user sees and sets the choice where they check for updates.

contracts.title: 4.15 · Stable installs use only the owner pin; development follows each release, with a durable channel that survives upgrades
contracts.description: ADR-0871 D1/D3. Fresh installs default stable, legacy owner installs retain development, and channel or stable-feed failures never select development. Tests: packages/app/src/updates/release-channel.test.ts and releases.test.ts.

reported.note: Targeted tests and pnpm gate passed on f9b89e8d: typecheck, ten affected packages and plan edges PASS. Real PowerShell bootstrap tests ran via STORYTREE_TEST_PWSH; real Windows installation remains increment_b51a820db8b2. No live pin published.

contracts.title: 4.16 · Pin an existing released build without rebuilding it, recording landed increment notes since the preceding pin and refusing a concurrent overwrite
contracts.description: ADR-0871 D1. The pin preserves original installer URL and digests, requires channel-capable delivery, refuses older builds and incomplete publications, and keeps increment identities so late closure records are included on the next pin. Tests: packages/app/src/updates/stable-pin.test.ts.

reported.note: Targeted tests and pnpm gate passed on f9b89e8d: typecheck, ten affected packages and plan edges PASS. Real PowerShell bootstrap tests ran via STORYTREE_TEST_PWSH; real Windows installation remains increment_b51a820db8b2. No live pin published.

contracts.title: 4.17 · A built main that cannot start leaves the running app as it is
contracts.description: Before the app that follows merged main restarts into a new build, it starts that build with --start-check, which loads its main process as far as registering its handlers and exits 0 without opening the library or using the network. A build whose check does not exit 0 within a minute fails as a failed build does (4.2, 4.9): the running app stays, its reason shows in the gear, that commit is not built again, and the next commit main moves to is built and checked afresh. A timeout reports whether the child spawned or exited, its exit status, whether its output pipes remain open, elapsed time, and bounded initial and final output. Refusing a timed-out check releases its output readers, so inherited pipes cannot keep the checker alive.

contracts.title: 4.18 · One storytree app per machine: setting up the app that follows main refuses where an installed app is present, and each app's start check refuses where the other copy is, naming its folder and how to remove it
contracts.description: ADR-0940 D1. The installed app is the Windows one-click install (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\storytree-0.3, marked by resources\storytree-installed; the packaging config ships no installer for macOS or Linux). The follow-main app is set up when a runtime slot under [home] holds a built app.

contracts.title: 4.19 · An installed app's releases.log keeps the update lines a person reads and stays bounded
contracts.description: The updater's blockmap dumps and duplicated-block warnings never reach releases.log, while the lines a person reads (channel, found version, downloaded, waiting with the install choice holding it, installs, errors) do; the file is rotated past a size cap so it never grows without limit.

contracts.title: 4.20 · The release signs the Mac build with the Developer ID and notarises it when the signing secrets are present, stays ad-hoc when they are absent, and refuses a signed build Apple could not notarise
contracts.description: The macOS package job's signing mode follows the repository secrets: no CSC_LINK keeps today's ad-hoc build with no keychain; CSC_LINK with Apple's API key imports the certificate into a temporary keychain, names the identity find-identity lists and notarises; CSC_LINK without Apple's credentials is refused. The release notes' Mac sentence says notarised only for a signed build. No step prints a secret.

contracts.title: 4.21 · An installed app knows it is installed (Windows by the installer's marker, a Mac by the delivery record naming its bundle) and follows published releases only on Windows or as a Developer ID signed Mac build
contracts.description: increment_502d51c10586. On darwin nothing is written inside the sealed bundle: the app is installed when it is packaged and $STORYTREE_HOME/delivery.json names its bundle as installDir, and its channel comes from release-channel.json. A development copy, a copied app or a bundle elsewhere is not installed. Following releases is a separate gate: Squirrel.Mac refuses an unsigned update, so an ad-hoc Mac build (every pull request's, and every release until the signing secrets exist) is installed but does not follow releases; the build records its signing mode in its package.json.

stories.title: The forest
stories.description: Each project is its own 3D forest that grows as its agents' work lands, and any story opens to explain itself in plain words. Every story is a story node: a flat island on a globe, cut into one territory per capability, each filled by what storytree verified about it (ADR-0804, ADR-0825 D3). The agents at work show at the capabilities they hold, and work done while holding no claim is listed beside the forest.

capabilities.title: 1 · Story nodes
capabilities.description: The forest keeps one story node for every story in the project: where the story sits in the forest, with its title and its overall health. Nodes follow the library, so a new story appears as a new node and a retired story's node goes, with nothing arranged by hand.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Three stories give three story nodes, each with its title and its overall health as the agent reports it.
1.2 · Adding a story to the library adds a node, and retiring a story removes its node.

1.3 · A story's place is its row by dependency depth and its slot in the row: the bottom row has the story most depended on in the middle and the rest outward, a higher row is ordered by where its dependencies sit, each row is packed round the globe's front with the sea gap between neighbours, and a loop in the dependencies never stops the layout (ADR-0839).
1.4 · A story's island sits north of every story it depends on; stories that depend on nothing share the bottom row; the rows run evenly from about 42° south to 42° north (ADR-0839).
1.5 · Adding a dependency moves the dependent's island up a row (ADR-0839).

1.7 · A growing island moves its row's neighbours along the row and nudges islands in other rows aside, each staying within a bound of its row position and clear of the rest; islands in other rows that fit never move (ADR-0804 D7, ADR-0839 D3)
1.8 · When a row no longer fits round the globe or nudging cannot make room, the globe's radius grows until no island overlaps another (ADR-0804 D7, ADR-0839 D3)

1.9 · A story's row is ranked by the stories its code's derived edges reach (with or without a capability at either end) together with its capabilities' recorded dependsOn rolled up to stories; package.json fields rank nothing; a project without a survey keeps the roll-up (ADR-0991 D2, D3).
contracts.description: A code edge the plan never recorded still places the island, a recorded dependsOn no import shows still lifts it, and a dependency only its package.json or its tests name no longer ranks it. Protected by packages/forest/src/planet-places/planet-places.test.ts: the proof surveys real package manifests and source imports, checks globe rows, and retains the no-survey plan fallback.

reported.note: Green: existing 1.9 now reads real package manifests through @storytree/forest/code-survey, proving code-derived rows and no-survey fallback.

contracts.title: 1.10 · A five-story forest opens with every nameplate readable, in a row and in a chain
contracts.description: At the app's default view, a five-story project whose stories depend on nothing (one row) and one whose stories each depend on the last (a chain) show every story's nameplate, each fixed to its island (ADR-0917): none faded, no two overlapping on screen, and every island facing the eye at least half on, not squeezed at the rim.

reported.note: settlePlates steps crowded plates down (ADR-0855 D1), plates wrap to 112 px (D2), opening faces the islands' middle (D3). In-page: row 5/5, chain 5/5, storytree 14/15 (Keys turned away), 0 overlaps.

contracts.title: 1.11 · A mapped story sits in a row below the mapped stories whose code imports it, by the survey's roads among mapped islands, and a built story sits above the mapped story its package depends on; a loop among them still draws every island
contracts.description: ADR-0993: new work stands on mapped islands. A mapped island has no capabilities, so a built story's package.json dependency on one ranks it (ADR-0991 D2, narrowed); between two built stories it still ranks nothing.

capabilities.title: 2 · Capability tree
capabilities.description: Each story node carries its capability tree: the story's capabilities, which ones build on which, and where each one stands, from planned through built to landed, and it grows as they land. Where a capability stands comes from two records kept side by side: the arc surface's rule for planned, in progress or landed, and the health the agent reports for its tests, always labelled as the agent's own.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A story with four capabilities, planned, being built, landed and reported passing, and landed with a failing report, gives a seedling, a seedling, a full green tree and a dead tree, in build order, each with the capabilities it builds on.
2.2 · A capability the agent reports red while it is being built stays a seedling.
2.3 · A landed capability with nothing reported is a pale tree.
2.4 · A story with no capabilities yet shows one seedling, so a new story is never invisible.

capabilities.title: 3 · Story node render
capabilities.description: The page opens in Forest mode, drawing every story node on the globe as a flat island cut into its capabilities' territories (ADR-0804 D1, D2) with the library core beneath them. Forest / Library switches this one globe (ADR-0660 D4): Library hides the story nodes and shows the knowledge points alone. You can turn and zoom in either mode, hover a visible artifact dot to see its title, and click a dot to read its summary in the right-hand story-panel slot (ADR-0661 D1/D2). Forest also lets you open a story by clicking its island. An artifact card and a story panel replace one another; Close and Escape dismiss the card. Switching modes preserves the scene, camera, rotation and zoom. Each launch defaults to Forest, with no saved mode. The flat forest and separate Look-inside view remain unavailable (ADR-0655).

contracts.title: 3.1 · The app opens a seeded project on the globe in Forest mode; its smoke check finds one story node per story, each drawn with its capability tree.
3.2 · A capability landing redraws just its story node, without a reload.
contracts.description: packages/forest/src/view/planet-update.test.ts protects the update calculation: an unchanged scene produces no redraw, and a change to one island preserves the other island object. These direct proofs do not claim mounted-browser execution; the mounted globe allocation is its separate increment.

reported.note: Green: existing scene/reuse implementation restored; both 3.2 proofs pass.

contracts.title: 3.3 · Clicking a visible story node selects it, opens its story panel and closes any artifact card.

3.4 · With nameplates shown (the default), each near-side story node shows its story's name, readable as the globe turns and zooms (ADR-0636 D4: in 0.2 the names lived on the 2D map the owner cut, so the 3D forest carries them).

3.6 · Every "builds on" link between stories, each one the code survey derives between two capabilities and each recorded dependsOn (ADR-0991 D1, D3), has exactly one continuous trail chain; shared trunks are drawn once and their width counts the original links.
contracts.description: The scene's links are the survey's derived capability edges together with the recorded dependsOn, one per pair: a recorded one is drawn by value, and a derived one no recorded one joins is marked type-only when only the code's types join the two capabilities. A derived edge with no capability at an end is a story edge with no road. Without a survey the recorded links stand.

contracts.title: 3.7 · A cross-story link docks at both actual clipped shores.
contracts.description: Its chain is its roads between islands, from dock to dock; the pathway build routes nothing inside an island (ADR-0951 D3, ADR-0836 D1). A lit lane goes on inland from each dock (world 6.8, ADR-0991 D4) along a way the forest finds when the lane lights, not in the build: the shortest way along lines already drawn on the island, the borders between its territories and the coast between two borders (a stretch of coast costing three times its length), whose last stretch runs along a border of the capability's own territory; the dock alone where it is already on that territory, and none where the island has no territory for the capability. No way crosses open land.

reported.note: 3.7 now passes with reversed 900:100 code shares; all 20 targeted forest/world geometry and layout tests pass. Forest passes local territory destinations through scene data; world has no forest import.

contracts.title: 3.9 · The globe's Stories and Library switches each draw their layer: both on, the islands over the core seen through the glass; Library off, the islands on a solid globe with no note points; Stories off, only the glass globe, the core points at their computed depths and the separated no-shelf artifacts, with every story node, name, claim, failure marker, selection ring, pathway and island overlay hidden; both off, nothing where the globe was and nothing pickable, the switches staying. With the Surfaces menu's Library off, only Stories is offered and the globe is solid.

3.10 · Each switch flips only itself, and every combination preserves the canvas, scene, core, camera, rotation and zoom. Stories off remains orbitable; switching it off clears story selection and its panel, and hidden islands cannot be picked; switching Library off closes a picked note's card. A new launch opens with both switches on.

3.11 · In the default Forest view a failing island (one with a capability storytree verified unhealthy, never the agent's report alone) is never hidden: opening spins the globe, level, to a failure; a far-side failure has an edge marker whose click reveals it, including after returning from Library. Library is the viewer's explicit choice to hide story nodes (ADR-0660 D4, ADR-0825 D3). Guided views may explicitly hide all island surfaces and their failure markers (ADR-0852 D5); restoring the default surfaces restores failure attention.

Forest rejects far-side dots behind the shell and dots behind land; Library admits every on-screen drawn dot. Off-screen or clipped dots cannot be picked, and movement of 5 CSS pixels or more is a drag rather than a click.

3.13 · Clicking an artifact dot opens its summary card in the right-hand story-panel slot and closes the story panel. Opening a story replaces the card. Close and Escape dismiss the card, and none of these actions writes to the library.

3.14 · Each capability is one connected, bordered territory on its story's island, its share of the island following its share of the lines of code (the island may grow to fit its files' circles, 3.19); Unclaimed code is its own territory (ADR-0804 D2, D3). In a project with verified health, before a code survey is available, capabilities share the island equally, with no file circles.
3.15 · Clicking a capability's territory selects that capability, as picking it in the story panel does (ADR-0804 D2)

3.16 · Every surveyed code file is one flat circle lying wholly inside its capability's territory and on the land, never overlapping another or stacked, spread over the territory's room; its diameter grows gently with its lines, 1.2 + 0.14·√lines (a 1,000-line file about 5.6 across), with no per-island scaling (ADR-0804 D3)
3.17 · Pointing at a file circle names the file, its lines and its capability (ADR-0804 D3)

3.18 · The land wears the session's traversal (ADR-0804 D5): the forest hands the knowledge core each file circle's place on the globe, and the surveyed imports between files, and a file circle the selected session opened is lit in the session's colour with the in-view ring (a compacted one lighter, no ring), and a capability's territory it opened is filled in the session's colour; everything else stays as it was.

3.19 · A surveyed island's land follows its story's lines of code, with a floor so a tiny story stays visible, and grows beyond that until its files' circles all fit at full size (3.16), its neighbours making room as any growing island's do (1.7, 1.8); an unsurveyed island keeps its capability ratio (ADR-0804 D3, D7)

3.20 · By default, each capability's territory is filled by its word (ADR-0744): healthy green, unhealthy red, and yellow while it is proposed or untested, except mid slate grey (#86939D) while it is proposed or untested and parked on purpose (ADR-0992); a claim never changes the fill. Unclaimed code stays neutral (ADR-0825 D3) A guided view may choose plain territory boundaries or hide territories explicitly (ADR-0852 D5).
contracts.description: Green for healthy, red for unhealthy, yellow while not proven and asking for attention, and mid slate grey (#86939D, at the other fills' opacity) when not proven and parked on purpose (ADR-0825 D3, ADR-0992). A claim leaves the fill alone; Unclaimed code stays dark hatched uncharted land.

contracts.title: 3.21 · A guided camera stop turns to a story, capability or file, or frames the core, over its requested duration; framing and a CSS-pixel side offset keep the target clear of a neighbouring card. A new stop or manual drag replaces the old motion without a jump, and a missing target leaves the view unchanged.

3.22 · A guided view independently switches sea, island grounds, roads, nameplates, territories, file circles, knowledge core and session tints; territories can show plain boundaries or health colours. Defaults retain the ordinary Forest view, Library hides the islands and keeps the glass, and hidden marks cannot be picked.

3.23 · The public forest view exports the app globe and its controls; screen-position reads locate a story, capability, file or core in canvas CSS pixels from the actual camera and globe rotation, including zoom, side offset and resize. Missing targets return no position and hidden, clipped or far-side surface targets report not visible.
3.25 · Saving a public Forest drawing replaces the saved snapshot only after its complete data is read; a failed read or write preserves the previous snapshot and leaves no temporary file.

Direct filesystem proof through the exported Forest snapshot module protects complete drawing data and capture time, replacement, failed reads and cleanup after a real rename refusal; Website owns its richer recording contents and offline presentation.

reported.note: Green: real save waits for complete data, replaces it, preserves failed reads, and cleans temporary data after rename refusal; legacy unused refresh wrappers removed.

contracts.title: 3.26 · Selecting a story lights each capability link between it and another story as a lane, derived from the code's imports or recorded alike (ADR-0991 D1, D3): "up" where it builds on the other, "down" where the other builds on it; links among other stories or within it stay unlit, a story edge with no capability at an end lights nothing, and with nothing selected none is lit (0.2's ADR-0242 one-hop highlight)

contracts.description: The website grows a recorded plan a stage at a time on one globe; within one layout each stage's islands keep their spots. When the host changes layout (the shop's first round at its own plan's places, then the finished shop's), the islands in both ease across once over 1.6 s, only their plates travelling and no roads drawn; an island new to the layout stands at its spot; reduced motion jumps.

Surveyed islands retain their existing verified territory presentation. Proof: render the same unsurveyed story planned then landed through the public Forest renderer and observe the visible change with no survey; vary reported passing, failing and not checked while the recorded work state and verified health stay fixed. Capture the existing Conduit planned and frontend tour stages on desktop and phone; the observer must be able to read the recorded landed share in the pictures.

reported.note: pnpm run test packages/forest/src/view/island-progress.test.ts now passes 2/2: real scene planned/claimed/partly landed/all landed across reported not-checked/passing/failing; placeholder excluded and surveyed islands unchanged. Browser rendering evidence still to be captured.

contracts.title: 3.30 · On a growing globe each territory fills in and each file circle swells as the growth schedules them, ending as drawn without one

contracts.title: 3.31 · Story names stay put on their islands as the globe turns, on a small globe as on a big one: where two shown names overlap on screen, the one whose island faces the eye less squarely fades and neither moves; the selected story's name always shows, a dimmed name yields to the names in focus, and a name under the Sessions strip fades rather than lifting

contracts.title: 3.32 · A selected story's capability names on the globe read without their number, each wrapped to at most two lines, and pointing at a capability's territory shows its full name and description
contracts.description: The owner, 2026-10-05: "On capability nodes we should remove the numbers, i dont think these are useful", and a capability's name "is the bit that needs more words to explain what that part does". The number stays in the record and the panels; only the globe's plates and hover drop it. A name longer than two lines ends in an ellipsis on its plate and reads whole on hover, with the capability's description beneath (increment_7ac3758dfbb3).

contracts.title: 3.33 · Where a selected island's capability names overlap on screen, the smaller territory's name fades and the larger's shows; neither moves
contracts.description: ADR-0917 D3. Seen landing increment_7ac3758dfbb3: Sessions over Claims and Context readings over Settings on The agent link at the old land size.

contracts.title: 3.34 · Zooming in past the islands hides them and every mark on them, leaving the glass and the core; zooming back out brings them back, a little wider than where they went, so they do not flicker

contracts.title: 3.35 · The live desktop forest draws its ordinary roads toward their destinations on opening and when dependencies arrive, while existing shared roads stay drawn and reduced motion is immediate

A normal first display starts undrawn and completes through visible intermediate frames; a real dependency update delivered by the desktop poll grows newly drawn spans while preserving established spans and all link identities. Unrelated description updates do not restart roads. Reduced motion shows the first road frame complete. This is separate from selected coloured lanes and recorded website replay.

Real desktop 3.35 passed in 28.4 seconds in the gate; numbered physical-front and live-window tests were observed red then green. Actual before/after captures preserve all 131 dependencies, normal first-frame zero, reduced-motion immediate completion, correct dependency direction, stable shared roads and no unrelated refresh restart.

contracts.title: 3.36 · A mini globe in the top right shows the land, the north and south poles, and a mark on the face you see, following every spin and tilt
contracts.description: ADR-0977: the mini globe is drawn as the globe stood at its opening, so it never moves: the land where it lies (near side solid, far side hollow), north at its top and south at its bottom, and a mark on the point of the globe facing the eye that follows every spin and tilt, sits at its centre when the globe is home, rises toward north as the globe tilts north, and shows dashed when that point is on the far side.

contracts.title: 3.37 · Clicking the mini globe or pressing Home eases the globe back to the view it opened on
contracts.description: ADR-0977: the opening turn, framing and side offset, taking the short way round; there is no double-click gesture.

contracts.title: 3.38 · The globe tilts no further than 50° toward either pole, and the wheel stops zooming out at half its opening size
contracts.description: ADR-0977: no drag, marker, guide stop or Home reaches a view from over a pole; spin stays free; the wheel's floor is half the globe's opening size, in Forest and Library alike.

contracts.title: 3.39 · A mapped story is drawn as one brown island, whole: no territories, no file circles and no hatch, brown used for nothing else; its land follows its lines of code up to a cap, so a very large one does not crowd out its neighbours; with no survey it is still brown land
contracts.description: ADR-0993 D3, D5; ADR-0992 D5. Mapped code was here before storytree and is assumed to be working: it carries no health colour, and it reads apart from parked work's slate grey.

contracts.title: 3.40 · While the right-hand panel is open, the globe glides into the free width left of it, zooming out only to fit, and glides back when it closes
contracts.description: increment_73f66f36cfe3: with the story panel or the Library's note card open, the globe's centre sits at the middle of the free width left of the measured panel (side offset minus half the panel's width plus its gutter), its turn unchanged; it zooms out only when the free width is narrower than the globe, and back to the earlier zoom on close unless the wheel moved it since. No move when the panel leaves no useful width, none under reduced motion's glide, none on picking another island while open. Home returns to the shifted pose while open; a resize keeps it centred; picking and rim marks follow the offset.

contracts.title: 3.41 · The page's locator places each drawn island and note on screen, faces one at once, and says when the glide is over
contracts.description: window.storytreeGlobe (ADR-1001 D1): each drawn island's story, title, capability count and client point with whether it is visible; each Library note's point; face(target) turns the globe to it with no glide (false when not drawn); still() is false until the globe hands over its controls and while a glide is under way. It only reads places and turns: the lag instrument's click still goes through the globe's pointer handlers.

contracts.title: 3.42 · The lag catalogue names each action, picks its island by name or size, and knows settled from what the page shows
contracts.description: @storytree/forest/actions (ADR-1001 D1, D2): the named actions on the forest's page with their steps, settled condition, budget (default 100 ms response, no frame over 50 ms, settled within 1 s) and time limit; chooseIsland picks the island with the fewest or most capabilities or a story by id or title; isSettled judges a page reading against an entry's settled condition. The lab run and the app's recorder read the same catalogue.

contracts.title: 3.43 · A built story whose package depends on a mapped story's has a road from its island to the mapped island as a whole, lit when either is selected
contracts.description: ADR-0993: new work stands on mapped islands, and a mapped island has no capabilities, so no capability road can reach it. The survey's package dependency (map 8.23) is drawn as one road from the built island to the mapped island, docking on its coast; a package.json dependency between two built stories still draws none (ADR-0991 D2, narrowed).

contracts.title: 3.44 · A pose the guide wrote but the page has not drawn still counts
contracts.description: The globe guide reads moving until the host draws the zoom and side offset it last wrote, and a stop, slide or home started meanwhile starts from that written pose, not the stale drawn one. A drag or wheel (cancel) hands the zoom back to the user.

contracts.title: 3.45 · The locator reads still only once the globe sits beside the panel as measured now
contracts.description: window.storytreeGlobe.still() is false while the panel width the page measures now differs from the width the globe last placed itself beside (a panel just opened or closed, whose slide starts after the next paint), and while that slide is under way.

contracts.title: 3.46 · Territories arrive without a flash: borders trace on, then the fill eases in
contracts.description: Inputs: an island's land built or rebuilt (a territory added during a replay or a live survey, or the territories surface shown). Outputs: the land is presented in its current mode before its first draw, so no territory shows a fill the view does not (no one-frame flash); what the island already drew stays whole across the rebuild; each new border traces on along its chain over one rendered second, at constant speed as the roads (world 6.17), then each new territory's fill eases in over 0.4 s. Hiding the territories forgets them, so showing them again draws on. Errors: none; under reduced motion, and as the globe first opens, everything shows whole at once.

contracts.title: 3.47 · Switching to the Library and back, and sweeping the mouse across the globe, answer within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, settled within 1 s or showing progress (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
contracts.description: The budget of the lag catalogue's library-and-back and hover-sweep actions (ADR-1001 D2, D5). No test in pnpm test names it: the Mint box's lag run writes its verdict, failing once a slowdown against the action's baseline reproduced.

capabilities.title: 4 · Drill-down
capabilities.description: Clicking a story node opens a panel that explains the story in plain words: its sentences, and its capability tree, each capability pointing at the ones it builds on, including any in other stories, named with their story. The tree has a space of its own inside the panel, where the user drags it around and zooms it; it opens zoomed out to fit the whole tree, as far as the least zoom allows, and an icon in that space's corner opens the same tree in a larger window over the forest, which opens fitted too. Each capability's card says proposed, healthy, unhealthy or untested on a strip coloured as 0.2 coloured those words, with the agent's report and storytree's as labelled marks (ADR-0743, ADR-0744). Clicking one of the story's own capabilities, in the panel's tree or in the larger window, shows it below the panel's tree: its sentences, its health as the agent reports it, and its contracts on request (ADR-0659).

contracts.title: 4.1 · A story whose third capability builds on the first two gives its sentences, its capabilities in build order each with its sentences and its health as the agent reports it, and a diagram with exactly two arrows.
4.2 · A capability that builds on a capability in another story shows an arrow to it, named with that story, and that capability's card says its word.
4.3 · A capability with no description says "no description yet" instead of leaving a blank.
4.4 · A contract the agent reported red, then green, shows "red, then green"; one reported only green says so.
4.5 · Storytree's own column shows beside the agent's report only where something wrote it.

4.6 · The panel shows the story's sentences and its diagram, and below the diagram only the capability selected: its word, its sentences, its health as the agent reports it, and its contracts folded until asked for. No front cover shows in it.
4.7 · When a story opens, the capability shown is the first in build order that has not landed, or the first if all have; one clicked stays shown, and a choice outside the story falls back.

4.8 · Each of the story's capabilities is a card you can click, marked when selected and tinted by its word (a healthy card edged green, an unhealthy one red), never by the agent's report; another story's capability is in the tree but cannot be clicked.

4.9 · The capability tree is a graph of fixed-size cards: each capability sits above the ones it builds on, and another story's capability sits one row below the capability that builds on it, not in one row with every other outside capability.

4.10 · Each card, another story's too, has a strip across its top saying its word, proposed, healthy, unhealthy or untested (ADR-0744), coloured as 0.2 coloured it (proposed amber, healthy green, unhealthy red, untested grey), and the agent's report and storytree's as marks labelled "the agent reports" and "storytree saw", storytree's only where something wrote it. The work state (planned, in progress, landed) is not on the card.

4.11 · The capability tree has its own space inside the panel, moved by dragging and zooming, with no scroll bars and never out of reach. It, and the larger window, open with the whole tree fitted in the frame and centred, never above full size nor below the least zoom; the larger window's "Fit" puts that view back. An icon in the panel space's corner, labelled "Open in a larger window", opens the larger window.

4.12 · The capability selected, when it is not healthy, says why under its word and who moves it (the agent, or you), naming the contracts that carry it; a contract whose last verdict was not re-run says "last seen failing <date>, not re-run since"; a healthy one says nothing more.
contracts.description: ADR-0825 D1 and D2 on the card: the library's derived reason (library 5.8) and the verdict an entry did not reproduce (5.7).

contracts.title: 4.13 · In a project whose health nothing verifies, a built capability's card and detail lead with what the agent reports, labelled as the agent's, and say storytree does not check this project's tests yet, never untested or who moves it
contracts.description: ADR-0630 in the story panel, for a user's project: a first user is not told tested work is untested and the agent's to fix (increment_ef066f718a63).

contracts.title: 4.14 · A parked capability's card keeps its word and reason and says it is parked, naming the arc
contracts.description: The drill-down carries the arcs that park a capability, and its detail says it is parked on them under its word and reason (ADR-0992 D6).

contracts.title: 4.15 · A mapped story's panel says it is mapped: here before storytree, assumed to be working, with its file and line counts, and shows no health
contracts.description: ADR-0993 D3: a mapped story carries no health reading of its own.

contracts.title: 4.16 · Opening a story's island, the smallest, the largest or the library's, answers within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, and its panel is open within 1 s or shows progress; closing the panel likewise (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
contracts.description: The budget of the lag catalogue's open-fewest-island, open-most-island, open-named-island and close-panel actions (ADR-1001 D2, D5). No test in pnpm test names it: the Mint box's lag run writes its verdict, failing once a slowdown against the action's baseline reproduced.

capabilities.title: 5 · Agent capability claims
capabilities.description: Shows on the world what each running session holds. Each capability claimed by a session that has a row in the running-sessions list (capability 7) carries one flag in that session's colour, standing inside the capability's territory (ADR-0968, which replaced the inset border band of ADR-0923 D1 and the outline of ADR-0825 D3). Each session has its own stable colour, the same on its flags and on its row, never the proven green or the needs-you amber. The flag keeps its size on screen and becomes a dot on an island too small to carry a pennant; it drops in with one ring at its foot when the claim arrives, stands still while held, furls and greys when its holder goes quiet, and lifts away when the claim is released or lands, with no movement under reduced motion. On an island with no surveyed code the claimed capability's equal share is marked as a staked lot, a dashed white line inside its border; a capability with no code on an island that has code draws nothing. No band, outline, fill or coast tint is drawn for a claim, so a territory's fill stays health's. A flag carries no visible agent name, reason text or hooks warning. It follows the agent link's claims and sessions, so a holder whose hooks have reported goes quiet after the quiet time; a holder whose hooks have never reported is never quiet as idle. Subagents and supervised lanes folded under a parent flag in the parent's colour, a session with no row flags nothing, and an increment claim draws nothing on the world (ADR-0923 D2). A growth replay flags the capabilities its recorded sessions held as it reaches them (contract 5.7). Missing hooks are reported by the agent link's setup check (capability 8, contract 8.5). *History: the wisps of ADR-0736 were removed by ADR-0804 D9; ADR-0825 D3 outlined a claimed territory and tinted the coast; ADR-0923 dropped the coast tint; ADR-0968 (2026-10-10) made the mark a flag and added lots.*

contracts.title: 5.1 · Session A claims "email form", and a flag in A's colour stands on that capability's territory, with no visible agent name or reason text; A's claim on a capability on a second island is flagged there too. An increment claim flags nothing, whatever its touches name (ADR-0968 D1, ADR-0923 D2).
5.2 · For a holder whose hooks have reported, after the quiet time with no new line its flags furl and grey; when A reports the capability landed, its flag lifts away.
5.3 · A session seen only through its tool calls keeps its flags unfurled even past the quiet time; the map draws no hooks warning.
5.4 · None of this changes how a capability's state is drawn.

5.5 · A session's colour is the same on every read, on its flags and on its row in the sessions list, and is never the proven-green colour. A subagent folded under its parent flags its claims in its parent's colour, and a session with no row flags nothing.

5.6 · A capability a running session claims carries one flag in that session's colour, standing in its territory at a constant size on screen (a dot where the island is too small); it drops in with one ring at its foot, stands still while held, furls and greys when the session is quiet, and lifts away when the claim goes, with no movement under reduced motion. On an island with no code the claimed share is marked as a lot. The flag is the only claim mark: no band, outline or fill, and no coast tint (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D1, narrowing ADR-0804 D9)
contracts.description: A claim is a flag so the fill stays free for health, and a claim shows even where the capability has no code yet.

contracts.title: 5.7 · Replaying a growth, the sessions recorded with the latest stage the replay has reached flag the territories they held, each flag arriving as the replay reaches it, none before the first (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D3)
contracts.description: A recording that carries each stage's sessions (as Conduit's does) is replayed as sessions passing over the islands: at each moment PlanetView draws the claims recorded with the latest dated stage the replay has reached, so a session's flags arrive when it claimed and lift away when it landed; nothing is shown before the first such stage, and the end shows what the recording ends with.

capabilities.title: 7 · Running sessions
capabilities.description: A see-through strip along the forest pane's bottom, spanning its width and collapsible by its header (contract 7.17) lists one plain row per session that has not ended, claimed or not (ADR-0749 D1; ADR-0737 D1's removal of off-plan rows and their evidence stands, and capability 6 stays retired), showing facts as labels and no prose on the owner's behalf: anything that needs the owner is an open question on the arc surface (ADR-0824). An unclaimed row is named from its harness and what it works in; a session working in several worktrees says so (D2). Each row shows what it is doing, its context bar and its available context total. Explicitly related subagents and supervised lanes fold beneath their parent behind “+N”. Each row has one expander (the same control as “+N”), closed at first; expanded, it lists each worktree the session works in (full path on hover) labelled unmerged or merged, the commands it started and has not seen finish, and the files in its window, read from the agent link's window reading (9.10) only when expanded, then its children. No row uses a state colour; each root row wears its session’s own colour, the colour of its wisps on the forest (capability 5, ADR-0736), and a hovered wisp highlights its row. Hovering or focusing a row lights its claimed islands and dims the others. Waiting rows stay plain, working and waiting read from each session's turns (ADR-0754 D5); rows neither working nor waiting are idle by their state alone, and are listed first under the strip's History tab rather than on Live, which a search box narrows (ADR-1002 D4); ended sessions are hidden. Parent relationships and totals are read only when recorded or supplied by the agent link; missing values are not guessed. *Narrowed in place, 2026-10-05 (ADR-0804 D9, decision_5aadb523c1cb; ADR-0923 D2, decision_027f3b08bb8b): no wisps are drawn, so a row's colour is the colour of its traversal and of its claimed territories' outlines, and the hovered-wisp clause no longer applies. Hovering or focusing a row lights only the islands holding capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (contract 7.4).*

contracts.title: 7.1 · The list includes once each session the agent-link reading lists (agent link 4.9, 4.12), whether or not it holds a claim: a session holding unmerged work stays even after it ended, while a verified close-out, or an ended or quiet session with no open work past the user's leave-after setting (1 hour by default, read as idle-after is), is excluded (ADR-0754 D4, ADR-0758 D3, D5, narrowing ADR-0749 D1 and ADR-0737 D1). Sessions at work come first and the rest fold into the idle row (7.10). A waiting row stays plain; working and waiting come from the session's turns (agent link 4.8), and only a session whose hooks report no turns is judged by the user's idle-after setting. A row's task uses its claim reason or held increment title; a session with neither is named from its harness and what it works in (its latest claim's branch, else its last folder), held to 40 characters, and never labelled off plan. A session whose lines name more than one folder shows how many worktrees it works in, naming them on hover (D2).

7.2 · An explicit parent relation or subagent-started record folds that child under its parent behind the row's “+N” expander (7.8), closed at first as every row is (7.8); expanding reveals its task and collapsing hides it again. No child is duplicated at the top. A recorded subagent lacking its own session reading is shown as observed, without inventing a live state; absent parent relations are never inferred from claim wording.

7.4 · Hovering or keyboard-focusing a row lights the forest islands containing the capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed, and dims the other islands; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (ADR-0923 D2). Leaving the row restores the ordinary forest appearance. With no claimed capability the row does not arbitrarily select one.

7.5 · Every row reserves an empty context-bar slot. When an agent-link context total is supplied the row displays that total; when absent it displays an unavailable mark, never zero. This increment draws no composition segments, thresholds or estimated totals.

7.6 · Each row's bar is its session's tokens used (agent link 9.5), read again every 10 seconds, on one scale for every row: 1,000,000 tokens across the full width (the display's choice; a reading has no window size, ADR-0728). A Claude Code reading's bar is split into Injected, Grounding, Implementation and Other in proportion to its composition (9.8), and hovering gives the tokens and each group's estimated share; a Claude Code row marks its reading's context guidance (the user's setting, 600,000 by default; ADR-0739 D1), one mark; a row whose reading carries no guidance has none; a Codex row is one raw segment with no marks. With 400,000 tokens split 2:2:3:1, the segments are 10%, 10%, 15% and 5% wide. The list's header names the four groups in bar order, each beside a swatch in its segment's colour.

7.7 · The list hands the knowledge core its rows as the core's roster, each row with its children in the row's colour. Clicking a row selects its session in the core and marks the row (a child's row selects its parent); clicking the selected row again clears the selection, and the core then shows no session's traversal. The list and the core share one selection (ADR-0738 D5, ADR-0921).

7.8 · Every row has one expander, an arrow at the row's start, closed at first, opening only when the user expands it; a row with children counts them as “+N” after its name (7.2's control, not a second one). Expanded, a row lists, under a small “Worktrees” label, every worktree it works in, oldest first, each by its folder's own name with its full path on hover and its merge label (7.15); then its “Running” block (7.16); then, under a small “Files” label, the files in its window (agent link 9.10), each once, in the order first opened, with files no longer in the window muted; then its children. Files are read from the agent link's window reading only when a row is expanded, never from a second reader; a session without a window reading says why and lists no files. Collapsing hides the detail and the children again.

7.9 · The running-sessions list shows facts as labels and prints no prose about a session: no 'needs you' chip or line, no close-out why, no 'holding unmerged' line. A row is idle, listed under History rather than Live and not counted in the header, by its state alone (working, or waiting within the idle-after time). Owner decisions surface only as open questions on the arc surface (ADR-0824 D1, D2, narrowing ADR-0758 D1; ADR-1002 D4).

7.10 · The Live tab lists only the sessions at work (working, or waiting within the idle-after time); listed sessions that are neither are not on it, and no "N idle" row stands for them. The header's count is unchanged. With idle sessions listed and none at work, the tab says "No sessions at work" and, as a button that opens History, how many are idle there; with none listed it says "No running sessions" (ADR-1002 D4, narrowing ADR-0758 D5; ADR-0824).

7.11 · A session whose close-out is unverified (a no, or a yes the facts disagree with) stays listed, and its row folds and counts by its state alone, showing neither a mark nor a reason for its close-out (agent link 4.12; ADR-0758 D3 as narrowed by ADR-0824 D1).

7.12 · A session holding unmerged work (agent link 4.9's open work) stays listed, even after it ended, wherever its row sits; its row prints no line about it, the fact showing only as its worktrees' "unmerged" labels (7.15) (ADR-0754 D4, ADR-0824 D2).

7.13 · When the listed sessions run on more than one machine, each row names the machine its session runs on (the latest its activity lines name), beside its name; when they all run on one machine, no row names one.

7.14 · A row whose session holds no claim is named by its app's title (agent link 4.19), held to the label limit, before falling back to its harness and place. Expanding any row opens with up to three lines describing it, from recorded words only: the app's title where the row's name is not it, the objective of the increment it holds, and the app's latest status. A row with none of these shows no description.

7.15 · Each worktree in a row's detail carries one short label from the branches its session recorded there: "merged" when none still holds open work; for an open branch with a pull request, "PR #n" and what it waits on (in merge queue, draft, failing, or in CI while its checks run), or "PR #n" alone when its checks pass or it has none; "unmerged" when no open branch there has a pull request read. The main line, or no branch, carries no label; a branch recorded with no folder is folded under the folder last worked in, and none is dropped.

7.16 · An expanded row's Running block lists the commands its session started and has not seen finish, background ones included, each by its first words (one line, ellipsised, full command on hover) and how long it has run.

7.17 · The list is a strip along the forest pane's bottom, spanning its width (up to 40% of the pane tall, scrolling vertically inside, never horizontally), see-through so the globe shows behind it. Its header (name, count, colour legend and a caret) hides and expands the whole list like the arcs bar's handle: it starts expanded, collapsed leaves only the header, and the choice is kept per project in the page's storage (a missing or foreign value reads as expanded). While the strip is open its header also carries a size control beside the caret, reading Expand or Restore for what a press gives and working from the keyboard: expanded, the strip (Live or History) fills the forest pane from top to bottom, covering the globe and its controls until restored, its rows still scrolling inside; the size is kept per project in the page's storage (a missing or foreign value reads as the usual height), and collapsing then opening the strip returns the kept size. Every row starts collapsed and its expander opens it (7.8), with no expand-all control; an expanded row lays its Worktrees, Running and Files side by side, in one column when narrow. At either size the strip keeps clear of an open story panel and of the stale-forest mark, and an open Arcs drawer lies over it.
7.18 · A session that has named itself is listed by its own name
contracts.description: A row is named by the session's own name (its latest, from the agent link's name_session or `storytree session name`) ahead of its claim reason, its held increment's title and its app's title; until it names itself the row reads as before, ending at harness · folder. Eventually consistent: a rename shows on the next reading.

contracts.title: 7.20 · A session the agent link flags for work on main wears it as a label on its row: a warning, "on main", for work outside a workspace; a neutral "first commit" while a new repository's first commit is pending; the reading's full words on hover; an unflagged row wears none (ADR-0906)
contracts.description: The forest's strip shows the reading's onMain flag (agent link 4.26) as a fact label on the row, never prose about the session (7.9), so work on main is visible on the strip as on `storytree session list`.

contracts.title: 7.21 · The History tab lists the idle sessions still listed, whatever the range, then the sessions the Live tab no longer lists that were active in the chosen range, outcome first
contracts.description: Beside Live, the strip's header has a History tab. It first lists every idle session still listed (7.10), whatever range is chosen, each led by the word "idle" where an ended session's outcome stands and otherwise drawn as its live row was: its labels, its context bar and total, and its expander with its detail and children (ADR-1002 D4). Then it lists once each session the live list no longer lists (a verified close-out, or an ended or quiet session past leave-after) whose activity, from its first line to its last, overlaps the chosen range, latest first, subagents excluded; with none it says "No sessions ended in this range". The range is Today, Yesterday or 7 days (local days, today included), or a custom from–to of days. Each such row leads with how it ended: "landed" with its pull requests (merged lines it held, and increments it closed as landed with their PR), else "held" with the title of a question its claimed increment is held on that was asked while it ran, else "closed out", else "ended without a close-out"; then its name (as a live row's: its own name, claim reason, increment title, app title, or harness and place), its agent, how long it ran (first line to last), and the stories it claimed work in.

contracts.title: 7.22 · Opening the History tab, changing its range, or searching it does nothing to the globe
contracts.description: The knowledge core's roster, the forest's wisps and island lighting are those of the live rows whichever tab is open, whatever range is chosen and whatever is searched (7.28); history rows, idle ones included, light no islands on hover or focus. The tab chosen is kept per project in the page's storage, as the strip's open state is (a missing or foreign value reads as Live). Owner, 2026-10-02; ADR-1002 D4.

contracts.title: 7.23 · Selecting a history row focuses the globe on its session as a live row does
contracts.description: Clicking a history row selects its session in the knowledge core (7.7, ADR-0738 D5), and the core's roster gains that one session, so it is drawn in its own colour; clicking the selected row again clears the selection, and the roster goes back to the live rows alone.

contracts.title: 7.24 · The sessions list and the forest re-read the plan only when their news holds a change to a story, capability, contract, arc or health record: news of other records, or of lines alone, draws from the tree they already have; their first news always reads.
contracts.description: Both re-read projectTree (~0.94 MB of Cloud SQL egress on 5 Oct 2026) on every news carrying any library change, notes and friction included, up to every 2 s while the app is open (arc_0ab31fd59c88).

contracts.title: 7.25 · Landing news refreshes the code survey without re-reading an unchanged plan
contracts.description: Merge log lines, landed increment closure lines and landed increment record changes request a fresh code survey. Surveys run one at a time, at most every 10 seconds; repeated requests coalesce, requests during a running survey converge afterwards, and failures retry. Unrelated log traffic and non-landed work changes request no survey. An unchanged survey causes no extra draw, and stopping prevents later surveys and draws. The existing first-read and plan-change refreshes and contract 7.24 remain.

reported.note: All eight forest-reading tests pass, including 7.25 landing triggers, preserved 7.24 tree reuse, ten-second coalescing, one running survey, retry/convergence, unchanged-survey no redraw, and stop during pending survey/tree. Evidence: night-G-increment_3fc264bab5a3.evidence/green.txt.

contracts.title: 7.26 · History's rows cost one pass over the log, not one pass per past session, so a live tick stays cheap however long the history grows
contracts.description: The sessions list rebuilds History on every live tick (each 2 s while agents work). On the laptop on 2026-10-08 a rebuild that walked every line once per past session took 5.7-11 s of a 50 s profile, one 400-600 ms frame per tick. Building the rows reads each line a bounded number of times.

contracts.title: 7.27 · A health change that re-records the state the tree already shows does not re-read the tree: news whose only tree changes are such health records draws from the tree held
contracts.description: Agents' test runs re-record contract health every few seconds, mostly unchanged. On the owner's laptop (2026-10-08) 27 of 42 live ticks in 90 s carried only health:updated changes, and each re-read the whole 665 KB tree (300-500 ms). A change to a state, or to a contract the tree does not hold, still reads it; an unchanged state leaves only its entry's time and author stale, which ADR-0836 accepts.

contracts.title: 7.28 · History's search box keeps the rows whose words hold every word typed, whatever the case
contracts.description: History carries a search box. It keeps the rows, idle and ended alike, whose words (name, agent, the outcome line with its pull requests or question, or "idle", and the stories it claimed work in, by title) contain every word typed, in any order and whatever the case. Emptied, every row returns; with no row left it says "No sessions match the search". What is typed is kept for the sitting only, never saved, and searching does nothing to the globe (7.22) (ADR-1002 D4).

contracts.title: 7.29 · Clicking a session's row answers within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, and the row reads selected within 1 s or shows progress (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
contracts.description: The budget of the lag catalogue's open-session-row action (ADR-1001 D2, D5). No test in pnpm test names it: the Mint box's lag run writes its verdict, failing once a slowdown against the action's baseline reproduced.

stories.title: The arc surface
stories.description: Over the forest, one read-only top drawer shows the project’s arcs as dense two-line lanes, with queued arcs behind their blocker’s caret and a bar for each root lane’s increments: what has landed, what an agent is on right now, what is queued behind other work, and what is waiting on you. Picking an arc opens its briefing, with what the arc is about and the questions waiting on your answer, and every state is worked out from what storytree has recorded, never typed in.

capabilities.title: 1 · Work states
capabilities.description: Every part, increment and arc shows exactly one state, worked out by one rule from the records, so no two views, and no two lines of one view, can disagree. A part is planned, in progress or landed; an increment, once closed, is landed or not completed (failed, withdrawn, or closed with nothing recorded), and before that is waiting on you, queued, held by an agent or open; an arc is waiting, blocked, claimed, idle, quiet, parked or closed.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A part no line names is planned. A claim makes it in progress, a landed report makes it landed, and a new claim after landing makes it in progress again.
