contracts.description: ADR-0966 D3 and D5: check:capability-list and check:plan-edges read the plan of the increment the branch names; check:capability-list fails a stale pending change, naming the history entry it was read at and the one that moved its record.

contracts.title: 7.7 · CI's plan-read account, granted exactly infra/library-host/plan-read-grants.sql, reaches the capability-list check's verdict, its stale pending changes included, as the owner does, and writes nothing
contracts.description: CI's capability-list check reads the plan on the Mint library as ci_plan_read (ADR-0952). Its grants live in the repository, and every read the check makes is run under exactly them, so a read the check gains without its grant fails here rather than in every pull request's CI (friction_e57f42834da8).

capabilities.title: 8 · Lag instruments
capabilities.description: The kept instruments that measure the app's lag (ADR-0836, ADR-1001), so every lane and re-measure compares before and after with the same instrument and the same seed: `pnpm lag:reads` times the page's reads over a throwaway Postgres with added latency per query, and `pnpm lag:desktop` performs the catalogue of named actions (opening the smallest, largest and a named story's island, closing the panel, Library and back, opening a Library note and a session's row, a hover sweep, idle) through real input on an instrumented copy of the desktop app, or the desktop page in headless Chromium over the stand-in bridge (`--chromium`, as on the Mint box), and prints each action's response, longest frame, settled time and IPC count against its budget, saying NOT RUN for any it could not perform. With `--against <ref | built app dir>` it measures this checkout's build and the other in alternating rounds on the same seed and says, per action, slower, the same or faster, with any read whose count differs as its own finding. The whole run queues behind the heavy-run lock. On the Mint box, `pnpm lag:box` runs it after merges rather than by hand (ADR-1001 D3): a systemd user timer every 15 minutes measures the newest main against each action's baseline, one bounded run at a time with the merges between skipped; a slowdown counts when a second run agrees, holds the baseline back, and is halved down to the pull request that caused it; the history sits in the storytree-lag database beside the library, which `pnpm lag:box` prints from any machine, and `pnpm lag:box rebaseline` accepts a cost with its reason. Never a gate: nothing of it runs in CI or a pull request's checks.

contracts.title: 8.1 · The read instrument delays every query a page read makes by the added latency and reports the read's query count and median time, the same count with or without the delay
contracts.description: `pnpm lag:reads` measures a page read under a fixed added latency per pg query on one seed: each query the read makes is counted and delayed, so a read's count is the same at any delay and its time grows with it, and nothing else (the seeding) is delayed or counted.

reported.note: Green step c27449d8 pins one full 40 ms requested wait per counted query and a generous 20 ms floor. Same contention reproduction passes; all 16 test units in full local gate pass. PR #501 awaiting CI/queue.

contracts.title: 8.2 · Desktop analysis reports the total and function times of a recorded CPU profile, matching each sample to its recorded interval
contracts.description: Replaying an actual V8 CPU capture through the desktop analysis entry reports every recorded interval once, with matching self and inclusive function times. This pins analysis of recorded execution; it does not attest a live Electron interaction capture.

contracts.title: 8.4 · pnpm lag:desktop judges each named action's rounds against its budget in one table, and an action it could not perform reads NOT RUN in the table and the exit code
contracts.description: From recorded rounds: median and worst response, the longest frame, settled, the IPC count, and within / missed / n/a against each budget on the worst round (settled past 1 s is within when progress showed within the response budget and stayed). NOT RUN carries its reason and makes the run exit 3; a missed budget does not. --analyze reprints the table from result.json.

contracts.title: 8.5 · The lag instruments seed one library in named sizes, and two seedings of a size hold the same content and make the same queries per read
contracts.description: lag-seed.mjs is the one seed lag:reads and lag:desktop read (standard; large, ten times as broad at the same depth). Two seedings of the standard size hold the same stories, capabilities, contracts, arcs, increments, questions, log lines and sessions, pinned, and every page read makes the same number of queries on each; the catalogue's fewest, most and named islands are three different stories on it.

contracts.title: 8.6 · pnpm lag:desktop starts the app on the seeded library by default and prints one table across the sizes it ran
contracts.description: Seeded (the default), the app's throwaway home names the seeded Postgres as its library, the address without the password and the password in auth.json readable by the user alone; each size's run is kept in its own folder and the summary leads with one table, a row per action and size. --live reads the real library through a copied home.

contracts.title: 8.7 · pnpm lag:desktop --against judges each action slower, the same or faster on both builds' medians, and prints a read whose count differs as its own finding
contracts.description: From both builds' recorded rounds of an action: each build's median of its measure (settled when it settles, else response, else frames over 50 ms), the difference, and slower / same / faster past MARGIN (20% of the quicker build and two frames, ADR-1001 D3). A read the action asks for a different number of times per round, the page's timer polls left out, is printed as a count finding. A side that could not perform the action makes the row NOT RUN naming that side.

contracts.title: 8.8 · pnpm lag:desktop --against performs each action's rounds on the two builds in turn, A, B, A, B, and one build's NOT RUN ends the action on both
contracts.description: The two builds take each round in the same minutes, so the box's load falls on both (ADR-1001 D3).

contracts.title: 8.9 · pnpm lag:desktop --against a ref measures it in a throwaway worktree installed with the repo's provisioning and removed afterwards; a built app folder is used where it is
contracts.description: The worktree is removed whatever happened, a failed install included.

contracts.title: 8.10 · pnpm lag:desktop queues the whole run behind the machine's heavy-run lock
contracts.description: No seeding, checkout or measuring starts until the lock is taken; a waiting run says whose run it waits for.

contracts.title: 8.11 · The box measures the newest main once it moves, one run at a time, the merges between skipped
contracts.description: pnpm lag:box decides from its recorded history: nothing while a run is going; once main has moved past the last commit measured, one run on the newest main against each action's baseline. Ten merges while one run is going produce one further run, on the tenth.

contracts.title: 8.12 · Each action keeps a baseline; a slowdown counts when a second run agrees; a re-baseline records its reason
contracts.description: An action's baseline is the last commit at which it was within the margin. A slower verdict asks for a second run, and only an agreeing one is a slowdown; the baseline does not move forward over it. pnpm lag:box rebaseline moves it with a recorded reason.

contracts.title: 8.13 · A slowdown is halved down to the merge that caused it, naming its pull request
contracts.description: On a slowdown that reproduced, the runner measures the merges between the baseline and where it was seen by halving, against the baseline, and names the pull request of the merge that slowed the action.

contracts.title: 8.14 · The history is kept in the library's server and pnpm lag:box prints it per action
contracts.description: Runs are written to the storytree-lag database beside the library (a run as it starts and as it ends), a project reading only its own; pnpm lag:box prints per action its baseline, last runs and any standing slowdown with its pull request, from any machine whose library is the box.

contracts.title: 8.15 · A run past its limit is stopped, recorded NOT RUN, and the heavy-run lock left free
contracts.description: Each lag run is bounded (default 30 minutes, the heavy-run lock's queue included); one that passes its limit is stopped through its process group, recorded NOT RUN with the reason, and never left holding the heavy-run lock.

contracts.title: 8.16 · After each measuring run the box writes each budget contract its verified verdict as a lag run, with the commit and the evidence: passing within the margin, failing on a slowdown that reproduced, not re-run when NOT RUN, and never failing on one noisy run
contracts.description: ADR-1001 D5, the shape of ADR-0825 D5: the harness, never a model, mints the verdict of each contract a catalogue entry names as its budget, so a slowdown that reproduced makes the owning capability read not healthy and reaches the health worklist. A slower verdict still waiting for its second run writes nothing, so a territory does not flicker.

capabilities.title: 9 · Code allocation guardrail
capabilities.description: Every pnpm test run, and so CI, refuses a checkout that leaves any source file of a story package reached by no numbered test (ADR-0838 D5), by running Guardrails' allocation rule (packages/guardrails, ADR-0911 D2) over this repository.

contracts.title: 9.1 · This repository leaves no source file of a story package unallocated, checked through Guardrails
contracts.description: Product behaviour (ADR-0623, ADR-0838 D5): every line of code on an island lies in a capability's territory. Runs as an always-run unit of pnpm test, so CI holds every pull request to it.

capabilities.title: 10 · A Mint lane runs on the engine its allowance allows
capabilities.description: Codex below 95%, Claude at the limit, one handover and a queue-preserving fast-fail exit. Founded on decision_2122230a3140 (ADR-0929).

contracts.title: 10.1 · Reads the newest allowance event in the eight newest Codex session files

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 carries the implementation for independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.2 · Expired allowance windows lapse, including windows dated from the reading

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 carries the implementation for independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.3 · Picks Codex below the configured 95 percent threshold and Claude when spent

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 carries the implementation for independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.4 · Honours an engine override before an unexpired exhausted marker

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 supplies independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.5 · Only a Codex usage-limit stop records exhaustion

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 supplies independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.6 · Runs the chosen engine in the current folder with login credentials and dated logs

reported.note: Corrected the macOS alias assertion to compare realpath. Focused tests and a Linux symlink-directory reproduction pass; full pnpm gate passes after merging current origin/main. PR #704 reruns independent CI.

contracts.title: 10.7 · Hands a Codex limit stop to Claude once with a carry-on brief and separate logs

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 supplies independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.8 · Returns the last engine exit code or 75 on a fast failure

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 supplies independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.9 · Reports overrides, exhaustion, allowance windows and the next engine

reported.note: Numbered test passes in the focused run and full pnpm gate; PR #704 supplies independent CI verification.

contracts.title: 10.10 · A Claude pick resting on a stale reading takes a fresh one first
contracts.description: When the engine would be Claude only because the newest Codex reading, over an hour old, says 95% or more, the lane runner runs one tiny Codex turn so Codex writes a fresh reading, and picks from that. An override, the exhausted marker, a fresh reading, or a reading that says the limit was reached is never probed, so Codex credits are never touched; status says when the next lane will refresh.

contracts.title: 10.11 · A lane that exits 0 having left no report or push is resumed once, then leaves residue and releases its claims

capabilities.title: 11 · The Mint pool keeps its lanes fed
capabilities.description: One survey of the library names every active arc's ready increments, oldest first and an arc no live session is on before a busy one, under the manager's skip rules (another machine, waits and held-on questions; the website arc is no longer skipped whole, increment_84b94c1f40b8); claims are the only conflict guard, and a refused increment is retried only once the refusing claim clears (ADR-0955 D2). Work this dispatcher ran whose session ended and which is back in the pool (it bounced on a capability claim, say) is offered again after a back-off, without a restart (increment_ac90da057d6c). Overtakes the night tracks' fenced feed (ADR-0931 D1), retired by increment_2c26fdf14cb0.

contracts.title: 11.2 · One survey reads every arc's increments, their holds and the standing claims
contracts.description: The pool reads the library once per look (ADR-0955 D2): one arcViews read and one holds read give every increment with its arc and the arc's state, beside the standing claims. Since increment_2c26fdf14cb0 it no longer reads sessions for laptop-touched arcs, which only the night tracks used.

contracts.title: 11.8 · The pool picks ready work from every package by claims alone, oldest first, an arc nobody is on before a busy one
contracts.description: pickPool (ADR-0955 D2): no fence or track is read; it skips closed work, parked arcs, live claims, waits, held-on questions, owner actions and another machine's work, and takes the website arc's ready work like any other arc's; it never starts one increment twice, and retries a refused one only once the claim that refused it clears.

contracts.title: 11.9 · An active arc with no open, unwaited increment and no open question is offered for planning, oldest first
contracts.description: feed.mjs pickPlan reads the survey's arcs (ADR-0955 D4): an active arc (the website arc included) whose every open increment waits (on work, an event or a question) and that has no open question qualifies; the oldest qualifying arc not already planned in its present state (11.20) is offered.

contracts.title: 11.10 · The pool takes ready work by its arc's priority, then by when it was parked
contracts.description: pickPool sorts ready increments by their arc's priority (1 first, unranked last), then oldest parked; the preference for an arc no live session is on applies only within one priority (ADR-0963 D2).

contracts.title: 11.11 · Work whose session ended without a hand-off is offered again after a back-off
contracts.description: An increment this dispatcher ran, whose session ended and which is back at proposal with no live claim, wait or held-on question (it bounced on a capability claim, say), is offered again once a back-off has passed since the dispatcher first saw the session gone, and not before, so a bounce is retried without a restart and a session that bounces repeatedly does not spin.

contracts.title: 11.12 · Work whose listed capability a live session holds is left out, and offered again once that claim clears
contracts.description: The pool skips an increment while any capability on its capabilities list is claimed by another live session, so it never starts a lane that can only back off; a held claim older than this dispatcher's start counts as the refusal, so the work is offered again as soon as the claim clears, with no back-off (increment_df249af40e10, friction_01f7af78ff23).

contracts.title: 11.15 · Only a wait for the owner or a held-on question keeps work from the pool as his; no wording in its body does
contracts.description: An increment whose needs line or body names the owner, with no wait for him and no held-on question, is picked; one with a wait for him is skipped with that wait's note as the reason.

contracts.title: 11.16 · Work is left out while a capability on its list is on the list of an increment another live session holds
contracts.description: The edit gate refuses a capability that sits on the capabilities list of an increment another live session holds (ADR-0949 D3), so the pool reads the same footprint: it leaves such work out, naming the holder and the increment, and offers it again once that claim clears, so a wide increment waits instead of spending lanes on back-offs.

contracts.title: 11.18 · Work whose lane was refused a capability is left out while any live session holds it
contracts.description: The survey reads the capability refusals of every capability a live session holds (directly, or on the list of an increment a live session holds), whoever refused it, each under an increment. An increment one of them names is skipped, even when the refused capability is not on its list, while any live session holds that capability, whoever it passed to, and the skip names the session holding it now; it is offered again once no live session holds it. Incidents: increment_8a3301a85e42, dispatched three times on 2026-10-11 with an empty list; increment_201f02e6baef, dispatched six times the same day as the capability passed between sessions (friction_5c71675a35f4).

contracts.title: 11.19 · Work whose machine field names another machine is left out, with that machine's name; work naming this one, or none, is picked
contracts.description: Inputs: a survey whose increments may carry a machine field (a short name from Machines) and this machine's name. Outputs: work naming another machine is skipped with "needs <name>"; work naming this machine or none is picked; on an unnamed machine, every increment that names a machine is left out (ADR-0982).

contracts.title: 11.20 · An arc planned in its present state is offered for planning again only once that state changes
contracts.description: feed.mjs planState reads an arc's open questions and each open increment with its status and holds; pickPlan skips an arc whose remembered state (`planned`) equals its present one, so an arc waiting on the owner is planned once until something on it changes (a newly parked increment, a different wait, work closing), however many surveys apart (increment_045b4e4377b1).

capabilities.title: 12 · The Mint pool's dispatcher runs its lanes under the box's cap
capabilities.description: The box's dispatcher runs through packages/dev-loop/src/lanes/launch.mjs pool (ADR-0955 D2, D4): one dispatcher at a time, filling free slots (the cap in night-max-lanes less the engines running) from the pool, each lane waiting for a slot and bringing the checkout to origin/main, pushing over SSH, under the shared lock, then running its composed brief through the lane runner; the stop file ends it after its running lanes. Founded on decision_2122230a3140 (ADR-0929 D3); the night tracks and the mintlib queue it once ran retired with increment_2c26fdf14cb0.

contracts.title: 12.1 · Each running lane's engine counts once against the box's cap
contracts.description: The cap (night-max-lanes, default 5) counts lanes: an engine started by another engine (Codex's node wrapper and its native binary) is the same lane, and a process that only mentions an engine (a wrapper script, a grep, a brief quoting 'codex exec') is none. A lane waits, a minute at a time, until fewer than the cap run, and says so once; it reads the cap on every poll, so raising night-max-lanes starts a waiting lane within a minute, with no lane ending and no runner restart.

contracts.title: 12.3 · One dispatcher at a time
contracts.description: The dispatcher refuses to start while pool.pid names a live process running launch.mjs pool; a dead dispatcher's leftover pid, or a pid reused by another program, does not block (holdRunner, which the watcher shares).

contracts.title: 12.5 · Each pool lane runs its composed brief on a prepared checkout through the lane runner
contracts.description: Under the shared night-checkout.lock, a lane waits for a slot, then brings [home] to origin/main, sets its push URL to [email]:storytree-ai/storytree.git (fetches stay on https) and installs. Its brief is the header, the increment's night-notes file when present, then the common brief; it runs through capability 10's lane runner with the box's add-dirs, and its start, engine and end lines go to the queue's status file.

contracts.title: 12.8 · The dispatcher fills free slots up to the cap and no further, never starts one increment twice, and retries a refused one only once its claim clears
contracts.description: runPool (ADR-0955 D2, D4): free slots are the cap less the engines running and the sessions still starting; it looks again when a session ends, and the stop file ends it after its running sessions.

contracts.title: 12.9 · `pool` starts each ready increment with the repository's pool brief, read-only work with the read-only rules
contracts.description: launch.mjs pool composes each lane's brief from pool-brief.md, or pool-brief-read-only.md when the increment's needs line says read-only or blind, under the shared lock.

contracts.title: 12.10 · The dispatcher restarts between sessions when the code it runs changes on origin/main
contracts.description: runPool reads the version of the code it runs in the shared checkout at start and on every look: one hash of the blob ids, at HEAD, of the files the dispatcher and the lane runner load (queue.mjs's POOL_CODE: launch, feed, queue, runner, engine, watch and the three pool briefs; ADR-0981). Once it differs, the dispatcher starts nothing new, lets running sessions end and exits 3, which the box wrapper re-execs; a change elsewhere in packages/dev-loop (the test runner, the gate, a test) leaves it starting work. When a survey fails or finds nothing ready and no session is starting, it brings the checkout to origin/main under the shared lock first (ADR-0955 D4).

contracts.title: 12.11 · With free slots and nothing ready, the dispatcher starts one planning session for a qualifying arc, at most one at a time
contracts.description: When free slots are open and pickPool picks nothing, runPool asks pickPlan for an arc and launches one planning session on it with the repository's planning brief (pool-brief-plan.md), never a second while one runs (ADR-0955 D4).

contracts.title: 12.12 · An increment handed to the watcher is not offered while its hand-off stands, its fix session running or not
contracts.description: The dispatcher reads the watcher's hand-off records and holds each handed increment as its event wait would, so the gap between the watcher clearing the wait and a fix session claiming the increment never starts a second session.

contracts.title: 12.13 · With free slots and nothing ready the dispatcher looks again within minutes; full slots poll, and a failing survey backs off
contracts.description: Idle with free slots: look again every two minutes (one bounded survey), so a newly parked or released increment does not wait a quarter hour; every slot busy: poll the slot count each minute without a survey; a failed survey: back off fifteen minutes.

contracts.title: 12.14 · The dispatcher remembers the arcs it planned, and their states, across its restarts
contracts.description: runPool records each planned arc with the state it was planned in through `plans`; the box's dispatcher keeps them in pool-planned.json in the lanes folder, so a restarted dispatcher starts no second planning lane for an arc whose state has not changed, and starts one once it has (increment_045b4e4377b1, friction_be96cb9391dc).

capabilities.title: 13 · A watcher lands a handed-over pull request
capabilities.description: A session on any machine ends once its pull request is open and its gate is green, and hands the PR to a watcher with no model (packages/dev-loop/src/lanes/watch.mjs): `watch.mjs handover <pr> <increment>` runs `hand` on the box directly, or over `ssh mint` from another machine with the session's own id, refusing with the reason when the box is out of reach (ADR-0974). `hand` records the hand-off in [home], sets an event wait on the increment so no other session takes it while it lands, and starts the watcher if none runs. The watcher polls GitHub: on MERGED it clears the wait, closes the increment landed with the PR and releases the session's remaining claims; on a red (a failed check, a conflict with main, or an ejection from the merge queue) it clears the wait and starts one fix session for that PR, which fixes, pushes and hands back; after its fix limit it writes an owner wait with the PR and the logs. The watcher (`run`) is a keeper over its look loop (`watch`), which exits with the restart code once the dev loop's code in the shared checkout changes, so the keeper starts it again on the new code. It is not an engine, so it counts against no engine slot; its fix sessions are. Founded on decision_e101df427118 (ADR-0955 D3).

contracts.title: 13.1 · A handed-over pull request that merges closes its increment and releases its session's claims
contracts.description: On MERGED the watcher clears the hand-off's event wait, closes the increment landed with the PR, releases any claim the handing session still holds, and forgets the hand-off.

contracts.title: 13.2 · A red pull request starts exactly one fix session at a time
contracts.description: A failed check or an ejection from the merge queue clears the event wait and starts one fix session for the PR; while it runs no other starts, and a fix that pushes a new head is judged on the new head's checks.

contracts.title: 13.3 · After its fix limit the watcher writes an owner wait with the PR and the logs
contracts.description: When the PR is still red and its fix sessions have reached the limit (WATCH_FIX_LIMIT, default 2), the watcher puts the increment on an owner wait naming the PR, why it is red and the fix sessions' logs, and forgets the hand-off.

contracts.title: 13.4 · A hand-off on disk survives a watcher restart
contracts.description: Hand-offs and their fix sessions are files in the lanes folder: a restarted watcher resumes each, counting a fix session whose process still runs as running, and one hand-off per PR keeps its fix count when handed again.

contracts.title: 13.5 · A hand-off parks the increment on an event wait and starts the watcher when none runs
contracts.description: hand <pr> <increment> records the PR, the increment and the session, sets an event wait so no session claims the increment while it lands, and starts the watcher unless a live one holds its pid file; the watcher is not an engine, so it takes no engine slot.

contracts.title: 13.7 · A session on any machine hands over, refusing plainly when the box is out of reach
contracts.description: `watch.mjs handover <pr> <increment>` runs `hand` on the box directly and over `ssh mint` elsewhere, passing the session's own id so the watcher releases its claims; with the box unreachable or no session id it refuses with the reason and the fallback (ADR-0974).

contracts.title: 13.8 · A handed-over pull request that conflicts with main is red
contracts.description: A pull request GitHub reads as CONFLICTING (mergeStateStatus DIRTY) is red even with every check green, so the watcher starts a fix session that merges origin/main instead of waiting for its three-day check-back; a mergeability GitHub has not yet computed (UNKNOWN) stays pending. From friction_fb05ce3cb334 (PR #1055).

contracts.title: 13.10 · The watcher restarts on its own code change
contracts.description: `watch.mjs run` is a keeper that starts the look loop (`watch.mjs watch`) from the shared checkout and starts it again whenever it ends (at once on the restart code, after a pause otherwise, and stops only when another loop holds its pid file). The loop reads its own code's version at start and before each look, and once it differs ends with the restart code between looks, starting no fix session after the change; fix sessions it started run on, and hand-offs on disk keep their count. Its own code is the files the watcher and the fix sessions it starts load, named in `WATCH_CODE` beside the loop (watch.mjs, queue.mjs, runner.mjs, engine.mjs), read with the dispatcher's `codeVersion` helper (ADR-0981 D3): a merge touching only other dev loop code (the test runner, say) leaves it looking. So a merged change to the watcher is in force on the box without a hand restart. From increment_a83e97065fa5 (four conflicting PRs stalled up to five hours on 2026-10-10 behind a watcher on pre-#1085 code), narrowed by increment_01a910c32f0c.

stories.title: Keys
stories.description: A user gives storytree a key once and every storytree process (the app, the command line, the MCP server) finds it: saved with `storytree auth set` into an auth.json in storytree's home that only the user can read, or pointed at the user's own store with a `!<command>` entry, with the vendor's environment variable as the fallback. storytree borrows a login the user already has wherever one exists and keeps a key only when nothing can be borrowed (ADR-0843). Its code lives in packages/keys (story id keys).

capabilities.title: 1 · Key store and resolver
capabilities.description: Keeps the keys storytree must hold in one auth.json in storytree's home, only the user can read and write it, and many processes can write it at once safely. It resolves a named key the same way in every process: an explicit value, then the file entry (a literal, or a `!<command>` run once per process), then the environment variable. `storytree auth set|list|remove` is its command-line front door: the cli family parses, calls this package and prints.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Saving a key creates `auth.json` in storytree's home (`STORYTREE_HOME` when set, else `[home], the folder `settings.json` uses), readable and writable by the user alone: on macOS and Linux the file's mode is 0600; on Windows it relies on the user-profile folder's own permissions, and nothing changes them.

1.2 · Two writers saving different keys at once both survive: reading `auth.json` back after they finish finds both entries, because every write holds a file lock and writes a temporary file that is then renamed over `auth.json`, so a reader never sees a half-written file.

1.3 · Resolving a key returns, first to last, an explicit value given by the caller, then its `auth.json` entry, then its environment variable: with all three present the explicit value wins; with no explicit value a saved entry wins over the environment variable; with neither, the environment variable is returned; with none, resolving says the key is not set.

1.4 · An `auth.json` entry `!<command>` resolves to the command's standard output, trimmed, and resolving it again in the same process does not run the command again; a command that fails is an error naming the key and that its command failed, which never contains the command's output.

1.5 · `storytree auth set <name>` reads the value from standard input, takes none as an argument and never prints it; `storytree auth list` prints each key's name and where it resolves from (file, command or environment) and never a value; `storytree auth remove <name>` deletes that entry from `auth.json`, leaving the others.

stories.title: The map
stories.description: An agent or owner focuses any project node to read its upstream dependencies and downstream dependents. The journey lives in packages/map and joins the library plan with the code survey read-only (ADR-0863, ADR-0864).

capabilities.title: 8 · Code survey
capabilities.description: Surveys story source packages and app frame paths (apps/desktop/src) for file ownership, source line counts and imports. Retains tests with numbered N.M titles and import edges, separately tagged as tests and excluded from source line counts. Ownership follows existing nearest numbered-test reach, execution coverage and type-import rules (8.1, 8.6, 8.7); unmatched files remain unclaimed. Lives in packages/map under ADR-0864; the forest consumes this survey for drawing. Callers may survey the current checkout explicitly. The main default reads immutable Git blobs from fetched origin/main, with shared bounded asynchronous fetches, keeping the last fetched main offline and reporting failure when none exists. No checkout is changed. Without origin, the primary folder is surveyed; non-Git folders are read directly. Unchanged blob identities retain file and story surveys. The forest owns request pacing; each later request checks for the next landing, so no cooldown can swallow its only refresh.

contracts.title: 8.1 · A source file a test titled "N.M …" reaches belongs to capability N of that test's story, whether the test imports it directly or reaches it through any number of further ordinary imports and re-exports. When tests of several capabilities reach it, the capability whose tests reach it nearest (fewest ordinary imports away; a re-export adds none) owns it, then the one whose tests reach it that near most, then the lower number.
contracts.description: The disk-reader proof resolves a numbered test through its own package.json literal exports, including public subpaths. Relative and self-export imports retain the same name filtering, re-export depth, type reach and measured-coverage ranking; private paths and other packages do not acquire local import edges.

reported.note: 40806c36: all 19 Code survey proofs pass, plus foreground gate typecheck/12 affected units/plan edges. Historical actual alias replay 754/67597 to729/67597; same-base current alias replay756 to731. Relative import equivalents confirm existing allocation ranking.

contracts.title: 8.3 · A file's lines of code are counted for source files only: a test file, or a test helper under a testing/ folder, adds no lines to any file, capability or story.
8.4 · A relative import from one source file to another is reported as a link from the importing file to the imported one.
contracts.description: Import links come from real syntax, including static imports, literal dynamic imports and re-exports. Quoted fixture text and comments create no links or ownership even when their paths resolve to actual source files.

reported.note: Final PR #553 head 70c8bf8acf3ef16374ab897aa46505c9b3353bbf uses @babel/parser solely to identify real module syntax and comments, with parseable-prefix recovery for unfinished edits. 15 focused tests pass; final foreground full gate passed typecheck, all 17 units and plan edges; guidance NOT RUN (unchanged). Exact paired readCodeSurvey removes Website collision, 1801/67836 -> 1805/67886 project unclaimed/total; 4-line Map residue is increment_1680b681eaed. Earlier TypeScript dependency experiment was removed after bundling checks rejected it. CI and merge pending.

contracts.title: 8.5 · Surveying again reads no unchanged file (same path and Git blob in a merged snapshot, or size and modified time on disk), reads changed files again, and reuses an unchanged story survey.
contracts.description: The survey may lag the checkout but must not re-read every file on every tree read (ADR-0836 D2): an unchanged story returns the same survey, a changed file is read and surveyed again.

contracts.title: 8.6 · A source file a numbered test's runs executed, in its own process or one it started, belongs to the capability whose tests executed it most (the package's coverage map); a direct import outranks it, and it outranks a file reached only through further imports.
contracts.description: ADR-0838 D3: where import tracing cannot reach because a test runs the code in a process it starts (the command line's tests spawn the built binary), coverage allocates it.

contracts.title: 8.7 · A source file a numbered test reaches only through type imports (a file of types, or one imported only for its types) belongs to the capability whose tests reach it so nearest, then most; any reach by a value import or by running it outranks a reach by types.
contracts.description: ADR-0838 D4: a file of types has no code a test can run, so the imports that name its types allocate it, after every other reach.

contracts.title: 8.8 · Each surveyed story names the stories whose packages its package depends on, through any dependency field of its package.json.
contracts.description: ADR-0840 D2: the code's story edges, read by the map graph as inferred story dependencies (packages/map/src/graph.ts). The forest's rows no longer read them: since ADR-0991 D2 rows are ranked by the derived edges (8.18, 8.19). Protected by packages/forest/src/code-survey/read-survey.test.ts.

contracts.title: 8.9 · The survey includes apps/desktop/src files under the app story, attributing their capabilities by the same numbered-test ownership rules as package source files.

8.10 · The survey retains test files tagged as tests, their N.M numbered test titles and their import edges, without adding them to source file, capability or story line counts. Number lists are validated before expansion: at most 256 entries per title and 4096 per surveyed test file, counting repeated entries before deduplication; invalid or over-budget titles supply no proof identities and do not stop other files from surveying.
contracts.description: Numbered proof calls remain visible after quote-bearing regular-expression literals; text inside a regex cannot supply a proof title. The regression checks complete files and files with an unfinished trailing function, retaining real import edges and source ownership. Ranges must ascend within one capability and use safe-integer endpoints. Each title is checked in full against its title budget and the remaining file budget before any range is enumerated; rejected titles consume no expansion budget. A file budget includes titles inherited from imported behaviour suites. Limits bound expansion work before deduplication, including repeated and overlapping ranges. Ordinary package-qualified identities, file imports and unrelated file surveys remain available. The 256-entry title allowance is generous against the largest six-entry range observed in repository test sources at a29b7f1b; the 4096-entry file allowance permits sixteen full title budgets while bounding aggregate expansion.

reported.note: Correction to prior test count: all 11 in-memory Code survey tests pass (not 12). New regression covers quote-bearing regexes, fake regex titles and a trailing unfinished edit. Paired survey 825/67630 -> 825/67636; six added Map source lines allocated, no unclaimed reduction. Independent review checking 11 reweights of already-allocated Library/Agent-link files.

contracts.title: 8.11 · Selecting current surveys that checkout, including local changes. The main default surveys fetched origin/main without changing any checkout, follows subsequent landings, and shares bounded asynchronous Git work per repository. If origin is unavailable it retains the last fetched main; without one it reports failure. A repository without origin, or a non-Git folder, keeps the primary-folder reading.

8.12 · A CommonJS `require` of a string naming a relative file, or the package's own exported subpath, is an ordinary import: a test reaches what it requires and everything that requires in turn, so a CommonJS package's files fall in the capabilities whose tests reach them

reported.note: red (require reached nothing), green; shop final commit places 30/33 files

contracts.title: 8.13 · A numbered test outside the package’s src reaches its source as a test in src would; outside src the reader follows test files and their helper dependencies within the package, without counting their lines as source or reading unrelated scripts
contracts.description: A project whose stories keep their tests in a test/ folder (the rebuilt shop, shop2) has its files allocated to capabilities, so its land carries health; helpers there add no source lines.

contracts.title: 8.14 · A test file that runs an imported behaviour suite carries the suite's numbered titles
contracts.description: A test file that imports a shared suite (a non-test file that itself imports node:test) is credited with the numbered titles that suite registers, for its retained titles and for ownership reach, so the map and the landing advisory see contracts proven by a suite each backend runs. Comments, quoted examples and files that register no tests credit nothing, and package prefixes keep their attribution.

reported.note: Suite titles credited; the real library memory/pg/cloud-sql tests now carry 2.1-2.13; pnpm gate PASS.

contracts.title: 8.15 · A source file's opening "Capability N · <title>" declaration (after a shebang) puts it on capability N's territory when N's numbered tests or coverage map reach it; a declaration they do not reach, or an undeclared file, is allocated by inference
contracts.description: ADR-0925 D1, D3: the survey honours a checked declaration, records each declared file's declared number and the capability numbers whose tests reach it (so the allocation rule can check it), and keeps ADR-0838's inference for everything undeclared.

contracts.title: 8.16 · A survey can be read on a worker thread: the same answer as reading it in place, while the asking thread's event loop stays free
contracts.description: The desktop app asks for a survey from Electron's main process; parsing every changed file there stalled it 2-4.2 s on the owner's laptop (2026-10-08), and the page's frames waited on it. The off-thread reader runs the same kept reader in a worker, so only the answer crosses back.

contracts.title: 8.17 · A changed file is placed in its capability by its own declaration, else by the survey's inference, flagged as inferred; a file in no story's package, or a file that cannot be read, is placed nowhere
contracts.description: ADR-0925 D4's lookup as one export of the code survey, so edit claims and the gate's capability-list check can never place a file differently.

contracts.title: 8.18 · A source file's import of a name from another story's package is an edge from its capability to the capability of the file that defines the name, type-only when every import behind it is
contracts.description: ADR-0991 D1. The defining file is found through the other package's exports (subpaths included) and its re-exports (named and wildcard); an import with no names (a namespace, a bare or a literal dynamic import, a require) reaches the file the specifier names. Imports in test files and test helpers make no edge.

contracts.title: 8.19 · A derived edge whose file at either end has no capability is kept as a story-to-story edge, naming the files that cause it
contracts.description: ADR-0991 D2: a story's edges are the union of its capabilities' edges, plus these, so no import across stories is lost when a file sits on Unclaimed ground.

contracts.title: 8.20 · A mapped story is surveyed from the folder this machine imports it from: the JavaScript and TypeScript files tracked at its checkout's commit under its folders, leaving out the skip list's folders and a folder another package of the same import maps, each with its non-blank lines and no capability, read without parsing; a mapped story whose import this machine does not name is absent
8.21 · A mapped story's package dependency on another mapped story's package is a road between them; a loop among mapped stories is reported with the stories round it, and refuses nothing
8.22 · Surveying again while an imported checkout is at the same commit reads none of its files and keeps each mapped story's survey; at a new commit only the files whose blob changed are read
8.23 · A built story's package dependency on a mapped story's package is a road from it to the mapped story; a mapped story's dependency on a built story's package is never a road
contracts.description: ADR-0993 D8, D9: new islands stand on mapped ones and import them; old code never imports new code, so the map reports no road that way whatever the old package.json names.

capabilities.title: 1 · Joined graph
capabilities.description: Read-only graph of plan, code and tests, owned by packages/map. Demonstrate Projects 2.5 reached from the desktop view file using a fixture plan.

contracts.title: 1.1 · The graph joins library stories, capabilities, contracts and declared capability dependencies with surveyed files, file ownership, file imports and numbered tests joined to their contracts, marking stored plan edges declared and survey or test-title edges inferred.

reported.note: Restored unchanged public graph export; all 9 graph/focus behavior proofs pass through the public graph entry, exit 0. Only final diff is graph.test.ts import path. Actual same-plan Code survey allocates four entry lines to Focus selection under existing rules; 829/67611 -> 825/67611 unclaimed/total. Log [home]

capabilities.title: 2 · Focus selection
capabilities.description: Select any file, capability, promise or story by upstream and downstream dependency depth and node kind.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Given either a code file or a capability as input, up returns its dependencies and down returns its dependents to the requested depth, with each returned node once at its nearest depth.

2.2 · Selection accepts file paths, capability ids or numbers, promise ids or numbers and story names; kind filters the returned node kinds without stopping traversal through other kinds, and an absent or ambiguous selection is refused explicitly.
2.3 · In a fixture plan where apps/desktop/src/view/view.ts belongs to the app Projects capability, selecting that file with up 1 returns Projects and its contracts, including Projects 2.5.

capabilities.title: 3 · Counts before detail
capabilities.description: Return complete counts and estimated token cost before detail; show every selected row or refuse above the ceiling, never truncate.

contracts.title: 3.1 · The default map answer gives counts by depth and kind, verified health tallies and the estimated token cost of the full answer, plus hints to narrow, without detail rows.
3.2 · Dry-run returns the selected row count and estimated token cost without detail rows.
3.3 · Show returns every selected row with id, kind, title, health, depth and edge provenance; above the safety ceiling it refuses with the counts and never silently truncates or ranks rows away.
3.4 · The map command exposes the same selection and counts, dry-run and show modes in text and JSON, including a structured refusal above the show ceiling.
3.5 · The agent-link focus tool accepts select, up, down, kind and mode counts, dry_run or show, defaults to counts, and returns the same complete-or-refused answer as the map command.
3.6 · In a branch's checkout the map reads the plan with that branch's increment's pending changes laid over; elsewhere the live plan
contracts.description: ADR-0966 D3: focus (and diff focus) in a worktree whose branch names an increment reads the plan with that increment's pending changes applied.

contracts.title: 3.7 · Focus on a mapped story, or on a file of an imported folder (by its path there or its full path), answers counts first with the word mapped in place of any health, and names a loop among the mapped stories it reaches
3.8 · The map command and the focus tool answer for a mapped story from the folder this machine imports it from

capabilities.title: 4 · Diff impact
capabilities.description: Focus a git diff on changed files, their promises and dependents, including the tests that name those promises.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Given a git range, defaulting to the branch against origin/main, affected joins changed files to their capabilities and promises, their downstream dependents and the tests naming those promises, using the map counts, dry-run and show modes.

4.2 · For each story whose package fetched origin/main changed within a given time, the newest such commit and when it was committed; a story whose package did not change then is absent, and with no origin/main there are none.
contracts.description: What the health worklist reads to hold back capabilities whose merge's own-health run has not recorded yet (friction_cf907de5ca3b).

contracts.title: 4.3 · The health worklist read at a checkout gives the library each contract carrying "no test names it" that a numbered test in its story's package on fetched origin/main names, with main's commit and its time; a test only off main names nothing, and with no origin/main none is named
contracts.description: The map's side of friction_c7a7e6754c54: reads which contracts main's tests name, for the library's worklist hold.

stories.title: Identity
stories.description: A first Storytree user signs in with Google, GitHub or Microsoft and is recognised by a Storytree-owned identity when returning. One journey in packages/identity (@storytree/identity), entered from the desktop or command line; the frame and CLI only mount or call it. Demonstration: sign in in the browser, return to Storytree, inspect the signed-in identity, restart and recognise it, then sign out. Feedback is a consuming app-setup journey.

capabilities.title: 1 · Portable user identity
capabilities.description: A trusted sign-in resolves to a durable Storytree user id. The identity-owned Cloud SQL users store retains linked provider+subject identities, the verified email and a replaceable WorkOS user pointer. Proof uses real PostgreSQL persistence to resolve first, repeat, linked and conflicting sign-ins without using email equality as identity.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A first trusted social sign-in persists a Storytree-owned user id, its verified email, the replaceable WorkOS user id and every linked Google, GitHub or Microsoft provider+subject identity; reopening the store returns that same user.
contracts.description: Proof: authenticate a signed fixture using the same token-verification path as the server, supply authoritative WorkOS user/identity evidence, resolve against real PostgreSQL, reconnect and resolve the same provider identity. Inspect the stored contact, WorkOS pointer and identity pairs.

contracts.title: 1.2 · A returning provider+subject identity resolves to its existing Storytree user id even if its email or WorkOS pointer changes; an unrelated provider+subject with the same email creates a different user.
contracts.description: Proof: resolve one identity, then repeat it with a changed broker pointer/contact and assert the original durable id; resolve a distinct identity with the original equal email and assert a different id. This is ADR-0874 D3's lock-in guard.

contracts.title: 1.3 · Authoritative linked identities join the existing user's identity set atomically; an identity set spanning two existing Storytree users is refused without changing either user.
contracts.description: Proof: resolve one provider identity, resolve authoritative evidence adding another allowed provider identity, then sign in through that identity and receive the same durable id. Plant two separate users and present evidence claiming both; assert refusal and unchanged records.

contracts.title: 1.4 · Concurrent resolutions of the same provider+subject create one Storytree user and return its same durable id.
contracts.description: Proof: two independently connected PostgreSQL callers resolve a previously unseen provider identity concurrently; both results have the same id and exactly one owning user persists.

contracts.title: 1.5 · The server resolves a user only from a valid WorkOS session token and authoritative supported social identity evidence; invalid, expired or wrongly issued tokens, unverified email, unsupported providers or missing subjects are refused before any user is written.
contracts.description: Proof: exercise the HTTP/server path with a correctly signed token and authoritative WorkOS user/identity response, then vary signature, expiry, issuer and evidence independently. The bad cases receive refusal and create no users. Raw caller-supplied email or identity claims cannot authenticate a person.

capabilities.title: 2 · Social sign-in and session
capabilities.description: The desktop and storytree sign-in use the system browser to authenticate through WorkOS with Google, GitHub or Microsoft only. The identity package owns PKCE/device-flow orchestration, trusted session verification, session persistence, status and sign-out; clients contain no WorkOS API key. Proof covers successful and refused exchanges plus a real authorized staging journey; production activation remains an explicit owner prerequisite.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Desktop sign-in opens the system browser with PKCE, offers only Google, GitHub and Microsoft, and completes only its matching authorization response; cancellation or a mismatched response leaves the user signed out.
contracts.description: Pending capability. Proof: desktop journey through authorized WorkOS staging, with callback-state and PKCE mismatch and cancellation cases at the identity package boundary; no WorkOS server secret is supplied to the desktop.

contracts.title: 2.2 · storytree sign-in shows the verification URL and user code, waits according to the device-flow interval, and reports the signed-in Storytree user only after authorization; denied or expired authorization leaves it signed out.
contracts.description: Pending capability. Proof: CLI device authorization against authorized staging and controlled pending/slow-down/denied/expired responses, through a thin command calling the identity package; no WorkOS server secret is supplied to the CLI.

contracts.title: 2.3 · A restarted desktop restores its protected signed-in session, refuses unavailable secure storage instead of saving plaintext tokens, and sign-out removes its session so the next status is signed out.
contracts.description: Pending capability. Proof: desktop session written through OS secure storage, restart/reload, status and sign-out; a storage-unavailable case writes no plaintext tokens. Neither status nor errors reveal session tokens.

contracts.title: 2.4 · A signed-in CLI reports its Storytree user without revealing tokens, and sign-out removes its saved session so the next status is signed out.
contracts.description: Pending capability. Proof: CLI sign-in/status/sign-out through its owned session store with captured output and a subsequent process; secret session material never appears in output.

verified.note: 3 of 57 tests skipped, at commit 394618153f72, run https://github.com/storytree-ai/storytree/actions/runs/38152269431

contracts.title: 2.5 · The desktop signs in only with a public WorkOS client ID configured, verifies WorkOS's access token itself against the client's published keys with no identity server, waits for the storytree-auth callback, and refuses a provider refusal, a failed exchange, a sign-out or a sign-in that never returns.
contracts.description: callbackSession adapts the official Electron SDK's main-process session manager (getUser: its validated, refreshed session) to DesktopSession. feedbackIdentityConfig offers sign-in only for a well-formed client_ ID; no identity endpoint (owner's choice D, a question: sign-in without a server for now). createFeedbackIdentity verifies the access token RS256 against https://api.workos.com/sso/jwks/<clientId> with audience storytree-identity (the JWT template), a user_ subject equal to the session's user, and the client if named; the email is the one the same code exchange returned, used only when WorkOS marks it verified, so the JWT template needs no email claim. A token or account that does not verify signs out; keys that cannot be fetched keep the session. signIn opens the system browser and settles on the storytree-auth://callback deep link: completed on a code exchange, refused on a provider error, a failed exchange, sign-out or a ten-minute timeout; a concurrent sign-in joins the pending one; a link that is not the callback is ignored. A callback that started the app is completed with no sign-in waiting. Only id and email leave the main process. Tested against a fake SDK session manager and locally signed tokens; live provider sign-in is separate acceptance.

stories.title: Journey events
stories.description: A user controls sharing of their named product milestones. All behavior and its consent/settings surface live in packages/journey-events; the desktop frame mounts it and the command line calls its public API. Demonstration: start with sharing off, opt in, complete an allowed milestone, observe a sanitized delivery, then turn sharing off and request deletion.

capabilities.title: 1 · Consent and allowed milestones
capabilities.description: Persist the user's default-off choice, anonymous installation UUID and strict event policy in packages/journey-events.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A new installation records no milestone while sharing is undecided or declined; explicit consent persists across reopen and enables only later milestones.
contracts.description: Proof: reopen one real local store through separate clients, try captures before and after opt-in, and inspect the queue/transport. No first-launch or installation event is backfilled from pre-consent activity.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Only the eight approved milestone kinds and their validated safe fields can enter the queue; unknown events, arbitrary properties and free-text error content are refused.
contracts.description: Proof: table of valid milestone kinds versus unknown kinds and hostile payloads containing paths, source, conversation or token fields. Stored payloads expose only policy-approved fields, including validated app version and categorical error codes.

contracts.title: 1.3 · An installation keeps its generated anonymous UUID across reopen and uses that UUID for its milestone identity; provider identifiers and tokens are never taken as analytics identity.
contracts.description: Proof: reopen preserves the generated UUID, captured milestones carry that identifier, and provider identifiers or token-shaped arbitrary input cannot replace it. Binding to a signed-in Storytree UUID and aliasing are explicitly deferred until the Identity sign-in integration exists.

contracts.title: 1.4 · Successful project creation and landed-increment closure record their milestones only while sharing is on; cancelled setup and other closure outcomes record none.
1.5 · A hooks-verified milestone is emitted only after the setup tool's existing four-hook check verifies the current session; incomplete or another session's evidence emits none.

capabilities.title: 2 · PostHog delivery
capabilities.description: Deliver sanitized milestones through the Node client to PostHog US (ADR-0908) with a small durable offline queue and bounded CLI shutdown.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A consented milestone survives offline failure and process restart in a bounded disk queue; a successful retry removes only the delivered entries.
contracts.description: Proof: injected transport fails then succeeds against a real reopened store; verify bounded queue behavior and retained/delivered identities. No live service credentials are used.

contracts.title: 2.2 · Delivery uses PostHog US (ADR-0908) through the Node transport with IP/GeoIP collection disabled and no added person properties; missing configuration performs no network request.
contracts.description: Proof: drive the real Node adapter against an intercepted request boundary and inspect destination, SDK configuration and payload. No client-side autocapture, raw IP or enrichment is introduced.

contracts.title: 2.3 · Turning sharing off clears queued milestones and blocks subsequent network requests, including another client's pending flush; CLI shutdown awaits a bounded flush.
contracts.description: Proof: two clients reopen shared consent state; pause delivery, opt out, then release it and assert no new request begins. Also assert shutdown waits for success or its deadline. Requests already accepted by the vendor cannot be recalled.

contracts.title: 2.4 · A shipped build is stamped at build time with only PostHog's public project token, which makes sharing available with its retention and deletion contact; a private key refuses the build, and an unstamped copy offers no sharing.
contracts.description: The release workflow supplies the public token (repository variable STORYTREE_JOURNEY_KEY) to the desktop main process and the released commands; the private personal key stays in Secret Manager for administrator deletions only.

capabilities.title: 3 · Sharing controls
capabilities.description: Offer an explicit first-launch choice and an always-visible settings off switch through a story-owned surface.

contracts.title: 3.1 · First launch offers an explicit consent choice with no preselected opt-in; unavailable live configuration is shown as unavailable and choosing decline leaves sharing off.
contracts.description: Proof: interact with the actual story-owned view and bridge, assert default control state and persisted choice. The notice names PostHog US (ADR-0908) and the named milestones/exclusions. Live sharing remains unavailable until all required configuration is present: public project key, owner-approved retention statement and deletion request contact. Missing any one of these cannot enable capture.

contracts.title: 3.2 · The settings surface always exposes the sharing state and off control; using the control persists off before acknowledging it and shows how to request deletion.
contracts.description: Proof: interact with the story-owned settings view, turn an enabled store off through its bridge, reopen the store and verify off plus discarded pending events. The frame only mounts the surface.

contracts.title: 3.3 · The CLI offers status, on, off and delete-request through the same persisted controls; incomplete configuration refuses on, and each invocation waits for its bounded flush without printing private authorization.

capabilities.title: 4 · Requested event deletion
capabilities.description: Let a user identify the events to erase and let an authorized administrative caller request their removal without distributing the private deletion key.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Requesting deletion turns sharing off, clears pending events and presents the installation identifier with the configured deletion contact without claiming remote deletion completed.
contracts.description: Proof: request deletion with queued events, inspect persisted consent/queue and returned installation identifier, contact and requested status. User-facing request handling requires no private service key; with no contact configured it truthfully explains that live sharing is unavailable.

contracts.title: 4.2 · An authorized administrative deletion call targets the requested person's events in PostHog US (ADR-0908); missing authorization sends nothing and responses never disclose the private key.
contracts.description: Proof: intercept the administrative transport, verify the selected identity and delete-events flag, exercise authorization absence/vendor failure/accepted asynchronous response, and assert results never include the supplied key. Real deletion and Secret Manager access require owner setup.

stories.title: CI health
stories.description: A user's project shows verified health from the test results its own CI already produced: storytree reads its CI runs on the main branch, matches each test to its contract by the contract number in its title, and writes the verified column (ADR-0901). Its code lives in packages/ci-health.

capabilities.title: 1 · Run results
capabilities.description: A CI job log's test output, read into one result per test (passed, failed or skipped) with the commit the run tested.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A job log's TAP, as the Actions API or `gh run view --log` prints it, reads as one result per test: `ok` passed, `not ok` failed, `# SKIP` or `# TODO` skipped, a subtest under the names of the tests it sits in; other lines give nothing

reported.note: red on a stub, green; reads all 63 tests from the shop's final archived log

contracts.title: 1.2 · The commit a run tested is read from its log's checkout (`git log -1 --format=%H`), and a log that names none gives no commit

reported.note: red on a stub, green

contracts.title: 1.3 · A job log in node's spec format reads as one result per test, as its TAP would
contracts.description: Node 23+ prints node --test results in the spec format in CI as well (the default reporter; storytree's own workflow pins Node 24). ✔ passed, ✖ failed, ﹣ skipped with its reason, # TODO skipped; a ▶ suite's tests sit under its title; the failing-tests recap at the end is not counted again.

capabilities.title: 2 · Contract verdicts
capabilities.description: Each test result tied to its story by the test file that carries its title at the run's commit, and to its contract by the title's leading number; each contract then judged passing, failing or not checked.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A result counts for contract N.M of the one story whose package's tests carry its exact title at the run's commit (its outermost numbered name); a title carried by two stories' tests, or by none, credits no contract and is listed as unmatched

reported.note: red on a stub, green; red again for the escaped-quote title the shop exposed, green after unescaping

contracts.title: 2.2 · A contract is passing only when it has tests and every one passed, failing when any failed, and not checked when one was skipped or none ran

reported.note: red on a stub, green

contracts.title: 2.3 · A test skipped on one platform for a platform reason counts passed when the same test passed on every job of the platform it needs; otherwise it stays skipped, and a contract a skip leaves not checked carries the skip's kind
contracts.description: Residue of increment_78b9102c9c81: agent link 4.10's hooks proof skips on Windows (platform:posix) and passes on Linux and macOS, yet CI health pooled the jobs and held it not checked, with no kind, so the worklist read 'no test names it'.

contracts.title: 2.4 · A result no test holds by its exact title counts for contract N.M of the one story whose test calls a helper with N.M and a title (contract("11.8", "…")), when the result's name begins with that number and ends with that title; held by two stories, it credits nothing
contracts.description: Tests built by a helper whose run title is a template the survey cannot read (`${number} [${backend}] ${title}`) still credit their contract, so health ci reads waits.test.ts's 11.1–11.8 instead of leaving them untested.

capabilities.title: 3 · Reading the project's CI
capabilities.description: The newest finished push run on the project's default branch, read through the GitHub Actions API, and its verdicts written to the library's verified column; the agent's reported column is never touched.

contracts.title: 3.1 · Reading a project's CI writes each judged contract's verified column, by the project's CI with its tally, commit and run, and only from the newest finished push run on the default branch; the agent's reported column is never written, so a capability the agent reports passing reads unhealthy when CI failed it, and healthy only when CI passed it

reported.note: red on a stub, green against the test Postgres

contracts.title: 3.2 · A project with no GitHub origin, or with no finished push run on its default branch, writes nothing and says why; its contracts keep reading not checked

reported.note: red on a stub, green

contracts.title: 3.3 · A job log holding terminal escape sequences is read all the same, whether gh refuses to print one unless allowed (2.102) or prints it as it is
contracts.description: gh 2.102 refuses to print a job log holding terminal escape sequences without --allow-escape-sequences, which older gh does not know; reading a project's CI passes the flag only when gh asks for it.

contracts.title: 3.4 · A story whose tests live in its package's own test folder, outside src, is verified from its CI as one with them under src is
contracts.description: Users' projects often keep tests in packages/<story>/test; their contract-numbered titles are read wherever they sit in the story's own package.

contracts.title: 3.5 · A job the run skipped, which has no log, is passed over: the run's other jobs are read all the same
contracts.description: GitHub answers a skipped job's log with 404 (seen 2026-10-04 on storytree's own skipped automerge job, 111309830646); reading the run must not fail on it.

contracts.title: 3.6 · A cancelled job with no log cannot hide available CI results; available cancelled-job logs still count, absent tests stay not checked, and other errors remain visible

3.7 · Each job's results are read as its platform's: a test skipped on Windows for a platform reason and passed on the Linux and macOS jobs verifies passing, and a contract a skip leaves not checked records the skip's kind
contracts.description: The job's runner labels or name give its platform, so the verified column credits platform skips and the worklist reason is honest (needs owner, out of CI's reach, not re-run).

contracts.title: 3.8 · A cancelled push run is passed over for the newest finished one that ran to its end
contracts.description: On a busy default branch a newer push cancels the run before it, often before its slowest job (Windows) has run its tests; reading that run leaves what only that job proves not checked. The reader skips cancelled runs and reads the newest push run that succeeded or failed, and says why when none did.

contracts.title: 3.10 · The merge queue's run of a commit the default branch holds is read in place of its cancelled push run
contracts.description: A project that merges through GitHub's merge queue has its push runs cancelled by the next merge; the queue's finished merge_group run of the same commit is read instead, so its verified health is not older than main. A queue run of a commit the branch never reached is not read.

contracts.title: 3.11 · Only the merge queue's run of the push run's own workflow is read, never another workflow's
contracts.description: The merge queue runs every workflow that listens for merge_group, and some (the capability-list check) upload no test results. Of the queue's runs of a commit, only the one by the same workflow as the default branch's push run is read, so a newer queue run of another workflow cannot leave health ci reading zero test results (increment_f5f73a43fef5).

contracts.title: 3.13 · A contract whose package the newest run's scope left out is judged from the newest run that scoped it in
contracts.description: Each run's tests are scoped to the packages its merge can reach (the 'scope:' line its log opens with), so a contract whose test merged reads its verdict from the newest default-branch run that ran its package, not 'no test names it' because the very newest run left the package out; a run that scoped everything in, or names no scope, ends the looking.

stories.title: Guardrails
stories.description: A user's project, or storytree itself, is held to storytree's rules: one package per story with roads running one way, and every source file of a story's package reached by a numbered test. One command, `storytree check`, reads the checkout alone and says plainly what breaks a rule. Its code lives in packages/guardrails, and storytree's own dev loop runs the same code.

capabilities.title: 1 · The package rule
capabilities.description: Refuses a checkout that breaks the package rule: a story with no package or a package that is no story's, a story's code in a declared frame or front door, a reach into another story's files, workspace packages depending on each other in a cycle, and a story depending on a declared frame or front door unless the owner sanctioned that edge; a sanctioned edge no package.json uses is reported.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A story with no package is refused, and so is a package that belongs to no story (in a project that declares no stories, every package under packages/ is a story's).

1.2 · A story's code in a declared frame or front door is refused; a frame test reaching the story through its package passes; a refused file that leans on the frame is never told to move into the story's package.
1.3 · A package reaching into another story's files is refused, by relative path or by a subpath its package.json does not export.

1.4 · Workspace packages depending on each other in a cycle, even through a devDependency, are refused (roads run one way). Each distinct cycle is reported once; shared acyclic paths are checked without path enumeration, including paths leading into a cycle.
1.5 · A story depending on a declared frame or front door is refused, naming the edge, unless the owner sanctioned it in the edge list; a sanctioned edge no package.json uses any more is reported.

capabilities.title: 2 · The allocation rule
capabilities.description: Fails a checkout that leaves a story package's source file reached by no numbered test, naming each such file with its lines and the three ways out (number a test, plan a contract, delete the code).

contracts.title: 2.1 · A story package's source file that no numbered test reaches (by import, or by its coverage map survey-coverage.json) fails, named with its lines and the three ways out; reached, it passes; a test with no number allocates nothing.
2.2 · A source file whose opening comment declares a capability its numbered tests and coverage map do not reach fails, naming the file, its declaration and the capabilities that do reach it
contracts.description: ADR-0925 D2: a declaration is checked, not trusted alone.

contracts.title: 2.3 · Asked to, a source file whose opening comment declares no capability fails, naming the file and suggesting the capability the survey infers for it
contracts.description: ADR-0925 D2's last clause: once every source file of storytree's own packages declares, the rule also fails an undeclared file and suggests the survey's capability. Switched on by storytree's own dev loop only; a user's project keeps working without the convention (D3).

capabilities.title: 3 · The check command
capabilities.description: `storytree check`, run in a checkout, runs the package rule and the allocation rule over it and reports every failure plainly, exiting non-zero, or says it passes and exits zero. It reads the checkout alone.

contracts.title: 3.1 · `storytree check` run in a checkout reports every package-rule and allocation failure plainly and exits non-zero; a checkout that keeps both rules prints that it passes and exits zero.
3.2 · It needs no plan, library or running app: it reads the checkout alone.
3.3 · Run from storytree's source on a folder, as a user's CI runs it, the check prints its report and exits 1 when either rule is broken, 0 when both are kept
3.4 · A project whose package depends on an imported app outside it, by link: and deep file paths, passes the check; a rule broken inside the project still fails it
contracts.description: ADR-0993 D1, D8: the check reads only the project, so an imported app's own shape (unallocated code, its own loops) never fails it.

capabilities.title: 4 · Graduated checks
capabilities.description: Deterministic checks on a change, run from a checkout far more often than CI runs. Each is all of a quality control check, or the part of one that is a fixed pattern, graduated from the Quality assurance story's reviewer (ADR-0956 D5). Run on the files a branch changes against origin/main, it reports every place a graduated check trips, by the check's name, the file and the line. It reads the checkout alone and records nothing: Guardrails does not reach the library, so Quality assurance runs it and records its hits in the QA ledger. If this capability grows too big it becomes its own story (ADR-0956 D5).

contracts.title: 4.1 · Run on a change in a checkout (the files its branch changes against origin/main), each graduated check reports every place it trips, with the check's name, the file and the line (for example a constant asserted equal to itself); a change that trips none reports none, and a tripping line in a file the change does not touch is not reported.
4.2 · It needs no plan, library or running app and writes nothing: it reads the checkout alone, and what it found is its answer, for the caller to record.

stories.title: Quality assurance
stories.description:
A change is reviewed before the gate, what the review found is recorded, and each check earns or loses its place on that record (ADR-0956). A reviewer with a fresh context (the `change-reviewer` role) runs quality control on a green change: it reads only the branch's diff against origin/main, the contracts the increment names and the quality control checks, and says which checks the change trips and whether the change does what its contracts say. Every review leaves rows in the QA ledger, in the library's Postgres, by check, project and package; the implementer answers each hit, fixed or rejected with a reason; the loop is bounded at ten iterations; and a check, or the fixed-pattern part of one, can graduate to a deterministic check in Guardrails, with its hits still recorded here.

Its code lives in packages/quality-assurance (ADR-0649). It sits below Session management (ADR-0969 D5): it may depend on the library, Guardrails and Session management's claims, sessions and log, and the MCP server, the command line and the dev loop depend on it.

Not in this story: any rule that samples, reduces or retires a check (ADR-0956 D6: nothing is built until the ledger holds numbers, and then the owner decides).

capabilities.title: 1 · Quality control checks
capabilities.description: A quality control check is one question a reviewer can answer yes or no about a finished change (for example: is any expected value computed the way the code computes it?). Each is its own artifact in the library, of the kind the library declares for it (the library story, Knowledge artifacts), linked to the principle or guardrail note it enforces; the notes stay, carrying the reason for the rule (ADR-0956 D3). This capability gives the checks as one reading, for the change-reviewer and for people, the same from both front doors.

contracts.title: 1.1 · The checks reading gives every live check with its question and, for each note it enforces, that note's id, kind and title; a retired check is not in it.

1.2 · The command line and the agent link's tool give the same checks reading, each through this package's public API; the tool is the one this package registers on the agent link's server, which serves it, and the review loop's tools, for every project, storytree's own or a user's.

capabilities.title: 2 · Change review
capabilities.description: The review of one change (one increment's branch) by the `change-reviewer` role, run as an ordinary subagent with a fresh context once the change is green and before the gate (ADR-0956 D1).
