This capability makes what the reviewer reads, the review brief: the branch's diff against origin/main, the contracts of the capabilities the increment names, and the live checks, with nothing of the implementer's reasoning. And it takes what the reviewer returns: for every check, whether the change trips it and where; for every contract, whether the change does what it says. The role's own text is an agent role in the library, a note, and is not contracted here.

contracts.title: 2.1 · The brief for a change's first review holds the branch's diff against the default branch origin names (origin/main when it names none), every contract of the capabilities its increment names, and every live check with its question, and nothing else: the increment's own body is not in it.

2.2 · A review's return is taken only when it answers every check in its brief (tripped or not, and where tripped: the file, the line and what was found) and every contract in it (met or not, and why not); a return that leaves one unanswered, or answers one the brief did not hold, is refused, naming it, and nothing is recorded.

2.3 · The command line and the agent link's tools issue the same brief and take the same return, each through this package's public API; the brief's tool takes the change's diff, or the worktree to read it from, as an argument, since the agent link's folder is not the branch.
contracts.description: quality_brief and quality_take beside quality brief|take (ADR-0793): the change-reviewer reaches its loop from either front door.

contracts.title: 2.4 · A contract the increment rewords through a pending change is in its brief in the pending text, marked pending, and one it retires through a pending change is listed as retired with its reason and is not to be answered; a return that answers a retired one is refused, naming it.
2.5 · The brief lists each contract under its story and capability, so two stories' contracts sharing a number both appear, each with its story
contracts.description: Every capability the increment names is a heading (story › capability) in the brief, even one with no contracts, and each of its contracts sits under it; a contract whose title carries no number is still listed under its capability.

capabilities.title: 3 · QA ledger
capabilities.description:
The record of what quality control finds, kept in the library's Postgres (ADR-0956 D4). Every review records, for each check it ran, whether it hit, and for each hit the implementer's answer: fixed, or rejected with a reason. Rows are scoped by check, project and package from the first row, because products differ in shape and a global count hides where a check matters. Its reading gives the counts per check per package, the same from both front doors. It only records: nothing here samples, reduces or retires a check (ADR-0956 D6).

Not settled by this plan (2026-10-10, raised with the dispatching session): where the rows sit inside the library's Postgres, as a record type the library declares, or as this story's own tables reached through the library's connection, as the agent link's activity log is. The contracts hold either way.

contracts.title: 3.1 · Recording a review writes, for each check it ran and each package the change touches, that the check ran there and each hit it made (the file and the line), with the review, the project and the time; a check that ran and did not hit is recorded as ran, and a second connection to the library's Postgres reads the rows back.

3.2 · The implementer's answer is recorded on a hit as fixed, or as rejected with its reason; a rejection with no reason, and an answer to a hit the ledger does not hold, are refused and nothing is written; a hit not yet answered reads unanswered.

3.3 · The ledger's reading gives, for each check and each package of a project, how many reviews ran it, how many hits it made, and those hits by answer (fixed, rejected, unanswered); a check that ran and never hit reads ran with no hits, never absent, and another project's rows are never counted.
3.4 · The command line and the agent link's tool give the same ledger reading, each through this package's public API; the tool is the one this package registers on the agent link's server.

capabilities.title: 4 · Review loop bound
capabilities.description: A review may loop: one iteration is one review and the implementer's answer to each finding. A change is not ready for the gate while a finding stands, which is a hit nobody has answered, or one rejected for a reason the reviewer has not accepted. After ten iterations with a finding still standing the loop stops and becomes the owner's question on the owning arc, which the session raises in ADR-0944 D4's order (ADR-0956 D7). It is a bound on disagreement, not a checklist to pass: the implementer's reasoned rejection is an answer the reviewer may accept.

contracts.title: 4.1 · A change's standing findings are the hits nobody has answered and the rejections no later review has accepted; a hit answered fixed, or a rejection a later review accepted, does not stand, and a change with none reads ready for the gate.

4.2 · From a change's second review on, the brief also holds each earlier hit with the implementer's answer to it, and the return must say of each rejection whether the reviewer accepts its reason; a return that leaves a rejection unjudged is refused, naming it, and nothing is recorded.

4.3 · Each review of one change is one iteration: with a finding still standing after the tenth, an eleventh brief is refused, and the refusal names the owning arc and the findings that stand, for the session to raise as an open question there; the refusal itself raises no question and releases no claim, and a change with no finding standing after the tenth is not refused.
4.4 · The command line and the agent link's tools record the same answer to a hit and give the same standing findings, each through this package's public API.
contracts.description: quality_answer and quality_standing beside quality answer|standing (ADR-0793): the implementer answers and reads what stands from either front door.

capabilities.title: 5 · Graduation
capabilities.description: Graduating a check moves all of it, or the part of it that is a fixed pattern, from the reviewer to a deterministic check in Guardrails (ADR-0956 D5). The check's record says which part graduated and where it is now enforced; the part that still needs judgement stays with the reviewer. Guardrails does not reach the library, so this story runs Guardrails' graduated checks on the change under review and records what they find in the QA ledger, under the check each graduated from.

contracts.title: 5.1 · Graduating a check, whole or in part, writes on its record which part graduated and the Guardrails check that now enforces it, and the checks reading shows both; naming a Guardrails check that does not exist is refused, and nothing is written.
5.2 · A check graduated whole is no longer in the review brief; one graduated in part stays in it with the graduated part named, so the reviewer judges only the rest.

5.3 · Recording a review also records what Guardrails' graduated checks find on the same change: each as ran, with each hit, under the check it graduated from, by project and package, marked as the graduated check's and not the reviewer's; the ledger's reading counts them under that check.

stories.title: The MCP server
stories.description: The MCP server is the second front door: the tool server an agent's harness starts, which serves every story's work as tools through one wrapper (routing the folder, naming the calling session, recording the call, ending merged claims) and hands the agent the habits card naming exactly those tools. It depends on every story it serves, and no story depends on it.

capabilities.title: 6 · Agent tools (the MCP server)
capabilities.description:
The toolbox the agent calls, served as an MCP server: plan work (arc, story, capability, contract), see the plan and who is on what, claim or release a capability, report a contract red or green, report a capability landed, say a capability is built so it is no longer proposed (`mark_built`, ADR-0744 D2), and search, read and write artifacts (plus list and add a node's front covers, once the library has them). Each tool is a thin wrapper over the library API and the claims above that answers in a short plain sentence the agent can act on, and every artifact read is logged in the agent activity log (ADR-0624); a new artifact with no place named goes onto the claimed capability's shelf of front covers (ADR-0627 D4, which redirected ADR-0624's default link).

As built: the 6.21 MCP cancellation checks cover claim, make_workspace and attach_workspace before and after library admission. They wait for their blocking and observing database connections to disconnect before removing the throwaway project. An admitted claim still finishes normally; this corrects the test teardown, not the cancellation contract.

contracts.title: 6.1 · A test client talks to the server inside the test itself, with no real agent and no network. It lists the tools, then plans an arc, a story, a capability and a contract, which then appear in the library's tree, the story and the capability each with its founding decision as the first book on its shelf, and it can correct each of them.

6.2 · It claims the capability and the increment it drives, sees both named with their holders in the plan and its data, reports the contract red and then green (the library shows the agent's report going from failing to passing, while the verified column stays "not checked"), and reports the capability landed, which ends the claim.
6.3 · Every call is recorded against the session that made it, using the session id the harness passes, and the machine it ran on.

6.4 · A bad call, such as an unknown capability, gets a readable refusal rather than a crash, and with storytree stopped every tool answers "storytree isn't running, carry on without it". If the database accepts TCP but never completes a fresh handshake, a tool call gives up at the 3-second connection deadline, including its library open, and says storytree is not reachable with what to check before retrying. A later call on the same tool server recovers when the database answers.

6.5 · An artifact written with no place named while holding a capability claim goes onto that capability's shelf as ADR-0627 D4 says, even with a newer increment claim; one with no capability claim gets no default place.

6.6 · Searching and opening an artifact leaves a log line saying which session read it, how it was found (a search result, a link from another artifact, by id, or from a shelf) and whether it took a peek or the whole artifact.

6.7 · Each read also names the agent that made it: a subagent by its id, type and task, or the orchestrator, as the harness revealed them (Claude Code through the hook's line for the call, Codex on the call itself), and "unknown" for a call the harness said nothing about.

6.8 · After Claude Code's `/clear`, which gives the window a new session id the tool server never sees, each call is recorded on the new session, as the hook before it named it; a call no hook saw keeps the id the tool server was started with.

6.9 · The test client parks an increment on an arc, starts it by claiming it, and closes it landed with its pull request, which ends the claim; the library shows each step and the arc reads closed. It records a landing that was never parked, parks a new increment on the closed arc, which re-opens it, and parks and unparks the arc.
contracts.description: After an increment is parked or closed, the response keeps the committed id and disposition explicit even if a follow-up arc read fails. It identifies that failed follow-up and preserves the library error recovery advice. A failed pre-write read remains a refusal and writes nothing.

reported.note: All three committed-write regressions pass, including the real MCP server with a schema-999 sibling and unchanged history on a pre-write refusal.

contracts.title: 6.10 · It sets a wait with a reason, and a claim on the waiting increment is refused naming it; it clears the wait, and the claim succeeds. A wait that would close a loop gets the library's refusal as a readable answer.

It raises a question on an arc and holds an increment on it, which a claim then finds waiting on the owner; it settles the question with his answer, which releases the increment; retiring a held question releases the increments held on it, naming them, and a record that is not a question is refused.

6.12 · It records friction with concrete evidence and a re-steer with the owner's quoted words, the agent's account kept apart; friction whose evidence is vague prose, a re-steer whose evidence quotes nobody, and a defect with no failure mode are each refused as a readable answer, and nothing is written. Shared capture stamps the calling branch and UTC date, and refuses a fourth friction report on that branch that day, counting routed reports too; the refusal names the cap and points to friction reinforce.

6.13 · It corrects an artifact's wording in place: the artifact keeps its id and takes the new words, only the fields given change, and an artifact that is not there, or a field its kind does not have, gets a readable refusal.

6.14 · It retires a contract and then a capability with a reason, and each is gone from the plan, its history keeping it. An id that is not a capability or a contract gets a readable refusal, and nothing is retired.
6.15 · Reinforcing friction through the tool or public capture function appends dated concrete evidence to the same item and preserves its route. Invalid recurrences write nothing.

6.16 · Every library write made by the tools names the calling session in history, including every record a compound call writes, increment starts, Claude Code's session after `/clear`, and Codex calls made by a subagent. A refused write leaves history unchanged, including a question whose requested holds include a missing increment or another record kind.
6.17 · Another story registers tools on this server beside its own, sharing project routing and the session log, and its short instruction line reaches the agent with the habits card.
6.18 · Another story supplies `land`'s final next line when needed, with none when it is not. A refused landing asks for none, and a failed follow-up keeps the successful landing explicit.

6.19 · It makes a workspace for an increment (`make_workspace`, 5.12): a worktree on a fresh branch from `origin`'s main, where Claude Code keeps its own, with the claim held by the calling session and the way into it named (`EnterWorktree` with its path); for work another session holds it gets a readable refusal naming the holder. For Codex, `make_workspace` instead returns instructions and the exact `ref` and `name` for the app's `create_worktree`, then `attach_workspace` takes that returned folder, ref and name and claims its verified branch. The agent uses the returned directory explicitly; an app registration error with a returned worktree is not a reason to create another. Attachment refusals say the app's folder is kept.

6.20 · An edit_plan call cancelled by MCP while its library write is still queued for the project write lock leaves the record and its history unchanged. A write already admitted completes normally and remains attributed to the calling session.

6.21 · MCP claim, make_workspace and attach_workspace calls cancelled before claim admission leave no held claim, claimed activity line or increment activation. A cancelled make_workspace creates no worktree or branch; a cancelled attach_workspace leaves the app worktree unchanged. Calls already admitted complete their claim, activation and workspace operation with the calling session retained in activation history.

6.22 · A test client calls `read_context` as session S and gets S's reading (session, harness, tokens used, when, source) worked out at the time of the call (9.5), including after S's transcript has grown with no turn ended; after a `/clear` whose hook named session T, the same call returns T's.
6.31 · `search_notes` answers with the library's ranked search (capability 14 of the library story), taking an optional `limit`, and says why when it fell back to words.

6.23 · `mark_built` switches a capability's proposed flag off once the agent considers it built, and back on (built: false), with the session as its writer; anything but a capability gets a readable refusal.

6.24 · A tool call a hook saw writes its `tool-called` line and every `note-read` it records naming that hook's `tool-requested` line as their cause, joined by the harness's call id. A call no hook saw names no cause, and nothing is guessed from timing (ADR-0746 D2).

`open` on a contract shows it whole: its title, its description and the capability it belongs to, as it shows an artifact; `open` on a question reads it whole, with its arc, state, wording, answer and the open increments held on it; an arc still gets a readable refusal.
contracts.description: An agent that finds a contract with search_notes can open it and read it whole (increment_c4b9051ec2de).

reported.note: Test 6.26 in agent-tools.test.ts; landed in PR #305.

contracts.title: 6.27 · `correct_question` corrects an open question's wording in place through the library's editQuestion (12.7): only the wording fields given change and it keeps its id; a settled question is refused with its answer standing, and a missing question or no words given get a readable refusal, with nothing written.
contracts.description: A session using only the agent link's tools can fix an unanswered question's wording, as `storytree question` / library edit can since PR #296 (increment_2d3b0027b274, friction_0805d54752f9).

reported.note: Test 6.27 in agent-tools.test.ts; red pushed, green on the increment_2d3b0027b274 branch.

contracts.title: 6.28 · `move_increment` re-homes an open or closed increment through the library, keeping its id, lifecycle, outcome, waits and any claim, with the session as writer and the reason in history; open work moving to a closed arc and missing records are refused without a write.
contracts.description:
The move gets both front doors (ADR-0793): the command line landed in PR #313 (storytree arc increment move); this is the agent link's half (increment_5e88ebc83dde).
After a move commits, a failed follow-up arc read keeps the successful move and its id explicit, names the failed read, and preserves the library recovery advice.

reported.note: Committed move remains successful with its id when its follow-up arc read fails.

contracts.title: 6.29 · `show_plan` gives each capability's word, and for one that is not healthy its reason, who moves it and the contracts carrying it, in its text and its data.
contracts.description: ADR-0825 D1, through the agent link.

contracts.title: 6.30 · health_worklist gives the oldest three capabilities on the health worklist, each with its reason, who moves it, the contracts carrying it and since when, and how many more wait; a capability an open increment touches is not offered, and one a test run in progress will record is held back, counted and named in its data, and the run named.
6.32 · name_session names the calling session, latest call wins
contracts.description: A session names its own row in the sessions list with a short one-line title (40 characters or fewer, as a claim reason is held), and renames it by calling again when its work shifts. A longer title is refused naming the limit. The command line's `storytree session name` does the same.

contracts.title: 6.33 · The built storytree-mcp command, started as a harness starts it, serves the agent's tools over stdin and stdout, and exits when stdin closes.
contracts.description: ADR-0838 D4: the tool server's entry point, which harnesses start for each session, proved as built.

contracts.title: 6.34 · A tool call a hook saw works in the folder that hook was run in, the session's worktree, not the folder the harness started the server in: a claim it takes carries that worktree's branch, so its merge ends it. A call no hook saw, or one whose hook named a folder of another project, works in the server's own folder.

6.35 · A re-steer whose evidence is the user's exact words without quotation marks is refused with the step that passes, putting those words inside double quotation marks, and the same words inside them are then recorded (regression: Conduit 3 on the reset laptop, 2026-10-02).
contracts.description: In Conduit 3 (packages/app-setup/evidence/first-build/runs/conduit-claude-turn-31.txt) an agent gave record_resteer the user's sentence verbatim, without quotation marks, was told to "quote what the owner actually said", retried with a shorter exact excerpt, still without them, and gave up: the re-steer was never recorded. The check is syntactic (a quoted excerpt), so the refusal says what it checks. increment_9f9bf0367bf5.

reported.note: Green on the laptop's full gate and on CI (Linux, macOS, Windows) for storytree-ai/storytree#490, merged 2026-10-02 00:43 UTC.

contracts.title: 6.36 · The daily friction cap counts each session's own reports: on a branch every session shares, as a user project's main, a second session's report is accepted after another session filed three that day, while each session is still refused its own fourth (ADR-0716 F2, narrowed)
contracts.description: From friction_2e6276b9582c: in the shop build the user project's sessions all worked on main, so session 1's three reports used the day's cap and sessions 2, 3 and 9 lost theirs, one naming a real defect. Reports whose writer was not recorded still count toward every session's cap.

contracts.title: 6.37 · `land` on a capability whose story's package, in the session's checkout, has a source file no numbered test reaches is refused, naming each file and the three ways out; no landing is recorded and the claim stays. Once every file is placed it lands (ADR-0911 D4).
contracts.description: Storytree names unallocated files inside the session, before CI, through the Guardrails story's allocation rule, the same code as `storytree check`.

contracts.title: 6.38 · land names each planned contract of the capability that no numbered test in its story's package proves, and still lands
contracts.description: Beside the unallocated-files hold (6.37, ADR-0911 D4), a landing reads the story package's numbered test titles with the map's survey (as CI health reads proofs) and names each of the capability's planned contracts none of them numbers, with the two ways out (write its test, or retire it). It names and does not hold: D4 holds only on unplaced files. Found by shop3 (friction_a193988ad179, increment_8ad908ef7bfe).

contracts.title: 6.39 · A tool call's reads do not grow with the log's length: the same calls (show the plan, claim, read the context, release) take about as much from the store in a project whose log holds weeks of history as in one whose log holds an hour's.
contracts.description: Measured through a byte-counting stand-in for the store. Red on main's source before #668: 30 KB against an hour-old log, 196 MB against 22 MB of history. Proven by packages/agent-link/src/tools/agent-tools.test.ts.

reported.note: Red on main's source (30 KB vs 196 MB); passes on main since #668.

contracts.title: 6.40 · It sets a wait for the owner or an outside event with a note, and a claim on it is refused naming the note; an event wait needs a check-back day; it clears the wait, and the claim succeeds
contracts.description: ADR-0938 D1, through the agent link's front door: set_wait and clear_wait take `for` (owner or event) with a note and, for an event, a check-back day, beside `on` and a reason.

reported.note: agent-tools-writes.test.ts 6.40 passes against local Postgres. Its red run was not observed separately: the tool change landed before the queued run started.

contracts.title: 6.41 · A tool reports each phase as progress the client receives before the answer, and a cancelled call starts no further phase
contracts.description: A tool's call can name the phase it is starting (call.progress); a client that sent a progress token receives each as an MCP progress notification before the answer, one that sent none gets the answer alone, and once the client cancels, the next phase's progress rejects so no further phase starts. Lets a slow call (the librarian's worklist) say where it is (friction_b0333dc7c3ff).

contracts.title: 6.42 · The close_out tool releases all of its calling session claims, reports the released ids in its text and structured answer, and reports no claims released when repeated.

6.43 · A tool called from a checkout not approved for the project its marker names is refused, saying how to approve it, before the project is opened or any line is appended; joining on purpose approves it
contracts.description: ADR-0942 D1: refusal comes before the project opens and before any tool operation.

contracts.title: 6.44 · Asking the owner releases the work it holds
contracts.description: raise_question holding an increment the session holds on the question's arc, or set_wait for the owner on it, releases the session's claims on that increment and the capabilities it took under it, and the reply names them; claims on other work stand, and a question on another arc releases nothing (ADR-0944 D4).

reported.note: releaseAsked wired into raise_question and set_wait for the owner; full local gate passes.

contracts.title: 6.45 · The tool server exits with code 0 when a delivery ran during its shutdown
contracts.description: The tool server's shutdown lets Node exit on its own once its close work is done, instead of calling process.exit while background work (a just-used fetch's WebAssembly parser still tiering up) is in flight; on Windows ARM that call aborts with exit 0xC0000409. A last-resort exit fires only if something still holds the process after a grace period.

reported.note: Red first on the Surface Pro 11 (Windows ARM, Node 24.19.0 arm64) with the old process.exit(0) shutdown: run 1 exited 3221226505 with libuv's async.c:94 assertion. Green 4/4 after the shutdown lets the process end on its own. On Linux, macOS and Windows x64 CI the test cannot go red: the abort is only seen on Windows ARM.

contracts.title: 6.46 · add_remedies adds live friction to a parked increment's remedies
contracts.description: A session on the agent link's tools adds friction to what an already-parked increment remedies, keeping those it had, so `route --to tool` accepts it; friction that is not live, or an increment that is not there, is refused with nothing written (the command line's 4.13, as a tool).

contracts.title: 6.47 · park_increment takes an increment's capabilities and links, and edit_plan replaces an increment's capabilities or links after parking; a story given as a capability is refused with nothing written (ADR-0949 D2)
6.49 · stale_claims gives the session manager each claimed increment whose holder is quiet, with its holder and route; reading it ends nothing
contracts.description: The agent link's surface of the stale-claim worklist (ADR-0953 D4).

contracts.title: 6.50 · plan_contract numbers a new contract past the numbers its capability's landed tests already carry, naming those no contract carries; a landed test's own number is kept
6.51 · edit_plan sets and clears an arc's priority, and show_plan lists arcs by it
contracts.description: The agent link's front door for ADR-0963: edit_plan takes an arc's priority, a whole number of 1 or more or "none" to clear it, refusing anything else with nothing written; show_plan prints each ranked arc's priority and lists arcs 1 first, unranked last.

contracts.title: 6.54 · A mounted verb's next steps are named as tools, below its sentence and in its data; a step with no tool is named as its command; an answer with none adds nothing
contracts.description: Tools give the same next-step guidance the command line gives (ADR-0786 D2: only steps that open a record the answer just named), worded as tool names, carried in the text and in the structured data for a harness that shows the agent the data (owner's answer to a question).

contracts.title: 6.55 · present_question marks a question as being put to the owner by the calling session
contracts.description: present_question marks an open question as being put to the owner by the calling session; another live session is refused, naming it, and open flags it; done frees it, and a settled question is refused. The agent link's door to agent link 5.36, beside the command line's question present (cli 5.13).

contracts.title: 6.56 · edit_plan and retire_from_plan, called by a session holding an increment, hold a change to a story, capability or contract planned before it as a pending change on that increment, leaving the live record alone; one the increment planned, or a call with no increment held, changes it live
6.57 · plan_contract adds an advisory line, never an error, when a contract's title runs past 300 characters, quoting the card's definition of a contract
contracts.description: 300 characters flags roughly the longest eighth of 338 live contract titles measured 2026-10-11 (median 168, p90 329). The contract is planned either way.

contracts.title: 6.58 · import_project imports a folder, given absolute or relative to the agent's folder, into the project as mapped stories, naming each one it added; a refused folder gets a readable refusal and nothing is written

6.59 · park_increment with waits_on parks an increment born waiting on another increment, so a claim on it is refused naming its blocker until that lands; a blocker that is not a live increment is refused with nothing parked
contracts.description: A later step of a chain parked through the agent tools is never ready for a moment before its wait is set, so the pool cannot claim it early.

contracts.title: 6.60 · every tool call's answer is recorded on the calling session as a door-answered line: the tool, answered, refused or failed with its class, and the next steps it offered as the tool door names them
contracts.description: ADR-0983 D1 (in force through ADR-0998): the tool server appends one door-answered line per answer, beside its tool-called line, so the front-door reading counts lines instead of parsing transcripts.

contracts.title: 6.61 · a tool whose door-answered line cannot be written still gives its answer
contracts.description: Recording an answer is observation: a log that refuses the line never fails or changes the tool's answer (ADR-0983 D1).

contracts.title: 6.62 · park_increment and edit_plan set an increment's machine to a machine Machines knows, edit_plan's "none" clears it, and an unknown name is refused with nothing written
contracts.description: The tool door to the increment's machine field: the name is checked by Session management's Machines before the library is written.

contracts.title: 6.63 · The tool server names every tool it serves
contracts.description: The tools a server would serve in a folder are listed by name without connecting to anything, the same names a client lists, so a reading counts the tools with no call.

contracts.title: 6.64 · check_setup from an MCP client storytree has no hooks for passes as connected, says what storytree does not do for it, and names its session id; a watched harness whose hooks are missing still reads as needing attention
contracts.description: Input: a check_setup call from a client whose name is not a watched harness. Output: data tier "connected", passed true, no hook fixes; text saying it does not see edits or commands, cannot refuse an edit to a held capability, has no context reading and ships no transcript, and how to give shells its session id (STORYTREE_SESSION_ID). A Claude Code or Codex caller reads tier "watched" and is unchanged.

contracts.title: 6.65 · A client that names no session keeps one session id for the tool server's life, or the one STORYTREE_SESSION_ID names in the server's environment, so its tool claims and its shell's commands are one session
contracts.description: Inputs: calls from an unidentified client, with or without STORYTREE_SESSION_ID in the server's environment. Output: every call recorded under the same session; that variable's value when set. Errors: none.

capabilities.title: 7 · Instructions (the habits card)
capabilities.description: One short text, a screen or less, that teaches the agent storytree's habits: plan the story first, claim a capability and open the knowledge it needs before touching it, write the failing test and report red, make it pass and report green, report it landed, and record an artifact for anything worth remembering. The tool server hands this text to the agent at the start of every session, as its instructions; Claude Code reads it from there. Codex (0.158 on) does not: it shows the model neither a tool server's instructions nor its tools until the agent searches for them, so connecting Codex also writes one short marked section into the AGENTS.md in Codex's home that sends the agent to check_setup before its first change in a storytree project and keeps it silent elsewhere (7.4; measured 0 of 3 without, 3 of 3 with, packages/app-setup/evidence/codex-first-session).

contracts.title: 7.1 · The text names every tool the server has, and no tool the server lacks.
7.2 · The text is no longer than 60 lines.
7.3 · The tool server hands the text to the agent at the start of every session.
7.5 · The card says who decides what
contracts.description: The card handed at session start names the kinds of decision the agent makes and records, the kinds it asks the owner about, that it checks the owner's standing delegations first, that the user's own instructions file (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) overrides that split either way, and the honesty promises no file moves: it never signs off its own output, never skips tests, and writes a question rather than only asking in chat (ADR-0842 D1, D2).

contracts.title: 7.7 · set_up_project's answer, and check_setup's in a project, carry the whole card, so an agent whose harness keeps only the start of the server's instructions (Claude Code keeps 2,048 characters; Codex shows none) still gets all of it.
7.8 · The card says what one contract is: a behaviour visible from outside, in what goes in, what comes out and the errors
contracts.description: Gives two planners the same test for where one contract ends, so one requirements file is not planned as 38 contracts by one agent and 5 by another (arc_424dae58bf1b, increment_412efdc2d4ed).

contracts.title: 7.9 · The card says how to build beside mapped code
contracts.description: ADR-0993 D4, D8 to D11: mapped code is assumed to work and changed only when named; new packages import it by link: and deep paths; old code never imports new code; test the interface; for a feature inside the old app bring in what serves its UI; before changing a middle part, find its callers and shape it with the user.

stories.title: The mark
stories.description: Anyone who meets storytree, in the desktop app, its installer, a taskbar or the public website, recognises it by one mark: a globe with islands, and inside the main island a tree of five dots, drawn in the colours of whatever surface it sits on. Its code lives in packages/mark (story id mark): one master drawing, its four colour roles, its named fixed-colour colourways and the icon files generated from it. Placing it on a surface belongs to that surface's story.

capabilities.title: 1 · Master drawing and colour roles
capabilities.description: One function from the four colour roles (ocean, land, tree, leaf) and an optional canvas to the mark's SVG text, so every surface draws the same geometry; and the named colourways (day, night) a fixed-colour file uses by default.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Given four role colours, the SVG fills each role's shapes with its colour and carries no other colour
contracts.description: Input: ocean, land, tree and leaf colours (any CSS colour, a CSS variable included). Output: the mark's SVG in a 104 x 104 view box: the globe in ocean, the islets and the main island in land, the tree's lines and its two inner dots in tree, the three outer dots in leaf, and no tile. Error: a missing role is refused, naming it.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Given a canvas or a named colourway, the SVG draws the tile in the canvas colour and the mark in that colourway's roles
contracts.description: Input: a canvas colour with the roles, or a colourway name (day, night). Output: the SVG with a 104 x 104 tile of corner radius 24 in the canvas colour behind the mark, and for a colourway its five colours. Error: an unknown colourway name is refused, naming the known ones.

capabilities.title: 2 · Fixed-colour icon files
capabilities.description: The PNGs (16 to 1024 pixels), the Windows .ico and the macOS .icns, in each named colourway, generated from the master drawing's shapes and committed in packages/mark/icons, so surfaces that cannot follow a theme use them.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Each committed PNG holds the mark rendered at its size in its colourway: the small-size drawing at 16, the master at every other size
contracts.description: Input: packages/mark/icons/<colourway>/<size>.png for each colourway and each size 16, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024. Output: a square RGBA PNG of that size whose pixels equal a fresh render in that colourway: at 16 pixels of the small-size drawing (ADR-0999: the master's own shapes and roles, the globe filling the tile, no islets, the main island and its tree 1.75 times larger with the tree's lines and dots bolder), at 32 and every larger size of the master unchanged; canvas at the tile's centre, ocean inside the globe, transparent outside the tile's corners. Error: a file missing or not matching names it and the regenerate command.

contracts.title: 2.2 · Each colourway's .ico and .icns hold the committed PNGs at the sizes Windows and macOS read
contracts.description: Input: packages/mark/icons/<colourway>/mark.ico and mark.icns. Output: the .ico's directory lists 16, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 pixel PNG entries; the .icns lists icp4, icp5, icp6, ic07, ic08, ic09 and ic10 entries (16 to 1024 pixels), each the committed PNG of that size.

stories.title: Reading the front doors
stories.description: The owner or an agent reads, for any window, how storytree's two front doors are used: every declared command and tool with its calls and sessions (those with none included), the words refused as unknown with the command each refusal named, door share per step, follows per offered step, and failures by class.

capabilities.title: 1 · The reading
capabilities.description: Counts a window of door-answered lines against the declared commands and tools: use per surface, misses, door share per step, follow per offered step with its like-for-like baseline, failures by class, each split by machine, harness and briefed or not.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Every declared command and tool is counted, those with none at zero
contracts.description: Given a window's door-answered lines and the declared commands and tools, each declared surface is listed with its calls and distinct sessions, a surface with no call at zero; a verb declared by neither door is listed apart, never dropped.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Misses: each word refused as unknown, with the command named and the rate per 1,000 calls
contracts.description: Unknown outcomes are grouped by where they were refused and the word typed, each with its count and the command the refusal named; each door's unknowns are also given per 1,000 of its calls.

contracts.title: 1.3 · Follow per offered step, beside its like-for-like baseline
contracts.description: For each next step offered, how often it was offered, how often the session's next call took it, and the baseline: how often the next call was that step after the same previous verbs when it was not offered (ADR-0786's measure).

contracts.title: 1.4 · Door share per step, and failures by class apart from refusals
contracts.description: Each call is put on a step (orient, search, claim, write, land, close, other) and each step gives its calls through each door; failures are counted per door, verb and class, and refusals (a no by design) are counted apart from them.

contracts.title: 1.5 · Split by machine, harness and briefed or not
contracts.description: Calls through each door, sessions and unknowns are split by the machine and harness the lines name, and by whether the session was briefed, read as a session given at most one prompt.

contracts.title: 1.6 · Reads a window from the project's activity log
contracts.description: Given an activity log, a project and a window, the reading reads only that window's door-answered lines and the prompts of the sessions in it, narrowed on the server, and counts them.

capabilities.title: 2 · The printed table
capabilities.description: Prints a reading for a person in a terminal (plain text, trailing 7 days with 28 beside it) and for a machine (--json), for the reconciliation increment.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Prints the reading as a plain-text table, the short window with the long beside it
contracts.description: Every command and tool with its calls and sessions in the short window and the long one beside it, the misses with the command each named, then follows, failures, door share and the splits.

contracts.title: 2.2 · Prints the same readings as JSON
contracts.description: The machine-readable form carries both windows' readings as the reading returns them, so a script compares numbers rather than printed text.

stories.title: Lag in real use
stories.description: The desktop app knows how fast it answered its own user: for each named action (the lag catalogue, ADR-1001 D1) it records the response, smoothness and settled time on the user's own machine into a bounded local file, and `storytree lag` reads them back against the budgets. All of it lives in packages/lag-in-use; the desktop frame mounts the recorder and the command line calls the report.

capabilities.title: 1 · Recorder
capabilities.description: In the page: recognises each catalogue action its user takes from the input and the page's settled seam, and records its response, long frames up to settled (count and longest), settled time, whether progress was on show, its name and a size hint, handing them to the app in batches only when no action is under way.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A catalogue action its user takes becomes one reading of its response, long frames, settled time, progress, name and size
contracts.description: Inputs: trusted inputs, the page's state each frame, and the browser's Event Timing and Long Animation Frame entries. Outputs: one reading per recognised action (name, response, long frames up to settled with count and longest, settled time, progress shown, size hint). An input that settles no catalogue action within its limit records nothing.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Readings reach the app in batches, never between an action's input and its settling
contracts.description: The recorder hands readings over only when no action is under way, in one call per batch; with the recorder switched off the page makes no call at all (ADR-0836 D1).

capabilities.title: 2 · Readings file
capabilities.description: In the app's main process: appends each batch of readings, stamped with the app's version and time, to a bounded file in the app's home (STORYTREE_HOME), dropping the oldest past 30 days or 5 MB. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is written to the library.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Readings are kept in one file in the app's home, the oldest dropped past 30 days or 5 MB
contracts.description: Each batch is stamped with the app's version and time and appended; past the age or size bound the oldest lines go; a torn or foreign line is skipped on read. Nothing else is written.

capabilities.title: 3 · Lag report
capabilities.description: `storytree lag`: per action, over the last seven days, the count, median, 75th percentile and worst of the response, longest frame and settled time against the action's budget, the worst action first, saying so when an action has fewer than ten readings.

contracts.title: 3.1 · The report prints each action's count, median, 75th percentile and worst over seven days against its budget, worst first
contracts.description: Readings older than seven days are left out; each row says how its worst compares to the budget; the action furthest over budget leads; an action with fewer than ten readings says so; with no readings the report says where it looked.
